press.text: Avalon, Borealis here. We share the Aval-Bore border, and in year one a bounce there only hands tempo to Cascadia/Grenmar. I propose a clean non-aggression pact through Year 1: neither of us moves against the other’s home centers, and we avoid cutting each other’s natural expansion. If you’re willing to leave Border Aval-Bore uncontested this fall, I’ll reciprocate by keeping pressure pointed east and can help keep Grenmar honest by sharing what I hear. If you need Aval-Bore for your plan, say so now; I’d rather arrange a demilitarized line than waste units bouncing.

Cascadia, greetings from Borealis. We can either waste Year 1 bouncing over Border Bore-Casc, or set a stable line and profit elsewhere. I’m interested in a practical non-aggression pact: no moves on each other’s home centers through Year 1, and coordination around the shared border so neither of us falls behind. My preference is to keep Bore-Casc peaceful and look west/north; if you have a specific opening in mind, tell me and we can avoid accidental conflict.

Deltara, we are not immediate neighbors, which makes us useful contacts. I’d like to keep an information channel open: if Cascadia becomes overextended toward you or me, we should compare notes. For now Borealis has no hostile intention toward you.

Grenmar, Borealis checking in. We are one step apart through Avalon, so our interests may align if Avalon overreaches. I’m not asking for commitments yet, but I’m open to sharing information and keeping the western side of the wheel balanced.

Borealis will be playing a straightforward board-balance game: agreements kept when they are concrete and reciprocal; no interest in chaotic early stabs that benefit third parties. If you want a demilitarized border or coordinated neutral plan, speak plainly and early.

Borealis — Cascadia is not looking for some globalist mess on our northern border. I want order and a clean non-aggression pact: I’ll secure Cascadia’s core and won’t move on your home centers if you don’t move on mine. We can keep Border Bore-Casc peaceful while you take care of your Avalon side and I handle Deltara. Confirm you’re not coming at Cascadia, and we’ll have a strong border and no needless war.

Deltara — I’m offering a straight deal: Cascadia secures Cascadia, Deltara secures Deltara, and neither of us wastes Year 1 throwing punches over Border Casc-Delt. No new foreign wars, no dumb establishment chaos. If you stay off my home line, I’ll stay off yours. We can revisit cooperation after Fall once we see who is honest.

Avalon — Cascadia has no quarrel with you. I’m watching the Borealis line closely; if Borealis gets too ambitious, we should compare notes. I’m for strong borders, fair dealing, and no backroom globalist gang-up.

Eastmark — you’re not on my border yet, but Deltara sits between us. If Deltara starts acting like an expansionist problem, Cascadia and Eastmark may have shared interests. For now I’m keeping my powder dry and my borders secure.

Fjordland — greetings from Cascadia. Early years are about who grabs neutrals and who lies. I’m not looking for distant wars, but I’m open to honest information sharing about threats on your side of the wheel.

Grenmar — Cascadia is focused on its borders and its people, not foreign adventures across the map. If Avalon or anyone else starts building a globalist coalition, I want to hear about it. Honest players can do business.

President Vance of Fjordland here. I’m not interested in a pointless early war on our frontier. My priority is Core Fjordland and a secure border, not marching into Eastmark homes. If you look toward Deltara and keep the Eastmark-Fjordland line quiet, we can both grow without wasting units in a bounce. Tell me plainly: are you willing to keep Border East-Fjor demilitarized this spring and discuss a fair fall arrangement?

Vance from Fjordland. We can either spend Year 1 bouncing over Border Fjor-Gren while Avalon gets fat, or we can make a real neighborly deal. I want a stable western frontier and no moves into each other’s home sphere. If you focus Avalon and your core, I’m prepared to keep this clean and discuss support later. Are you willing to avoid Border Fjor-Gren this spring?

Fjordland here. We don’t share a border, which makes us natural partners in keeping the wheel balanced. I expect Eastmark may try to play both sides. If you put pressure on your Eastmark frontier, you’ll find Fjordland has no interest in bailing Eastmark out.

Fjordland here. We’re not neighbors, but Grenmar sits between us. I’m looking for a stable west, not chaos, but if Grenmar overreaches I’m willing to coordinate. Keep me posted on what they’re telling you.
Fjordland’s position is simple: we’ll defend our borders, take care of our own core, and avoid any grand crusades. Neighbors who deal straight will get straight dealing back.

President Buttigieg here for Deltara. I’d like to open with a stable, transparent western frontier between us. My preference is no early Deltara-Cascadia war: we both have more to gain by growing cleanly and keeping forces pointed away from each other than by bouncing over Border Casc-Delt. Are you open to a Spring/Fall non-aggression understanding around our shared line, with advance notice before either of us makes a move that could threaten the other’s home centers?

President Buttigieg for Deltara. I’d like to avoid the familiar mistake of neighbors spending year one grinding each other down while everyone else expands. I’m proposing a straightforward Deltara-Eastmark non-aggression pact for 1901: no moves against home centers, no supported attacks across our shared frontier, and a preference for coordinated/transparent handling of Border Delt-East. If you’re interested, I’m ready to keep this border calm and predictable.

President Buttigieg of Deltara. We don’t share an immediate border, which makes this a good moment to establish a practical channel. I’m aiming for a stable opening and would value information-sharing about the Cascadia side of the board. If Cascadia plays cooperatively, great; if not, I’d rather we both know early and avoid surprises.

President Buttigieg of Deltara. We’re one step removed, but our interests may align if either of our shared-neighbor situations turns unstable. I’m opening with a preference for calm borders and responsible growth. I’d welcome a communication channel about Eastmark’s posture so neither of us gets caught flat-footed.

Deltara’s opening position is simple: predictable diplomacy, no surprise crusades, and a preference for negotiated borders over wasteful early wars. I’m available to coordinate practical non-aggression and information-sharing agreements.

President Newsom of Grenmar here. I’d like to start this map with clarity, not chaos. I’m proposing a non-aggression pact between Grenmar and Avalon: no moves into one another’s home areas, no supported attacks, and a good-faith effort to keep Border Gren-Aval from becoming the spark for an early war. If you’re willing, let’s coordinate neutral-center claims and keep our western frontier stable while the board develops.

President Newsom of Grenmar here. I’m reaching out early because the Grenmar-Fjordland frontier can either become a wasteful Year 1 trench line or a stable platform for both of us to grow. I propose non-aggression: no moves into each other’s home areas and no supported attacks. Let’s discuss Border Fjor-Gren frankly and avoid an accidental collision that only benefits the rest of the wheel.

Greetings from Grenmar. We don’t share a frontier, which makes this a good moment to establish a straight line of communication without immediate pressure. I’m interested in a stable rim, transparency about threats, and keeping any one bloc from rolling the board unchecked. If Avalon starts signaling aggressive designs in your direction or mine, I’d value comparing notes.

Greetings from Grenmar. We’re not direct neighbors, and that gives us room for a constructive relationship. I’m aiming for steady, rules-based expansion and durable partnerships rather than early chaos. Since Fjordland sits between us, I’d be interested in sharing impressions if they begin overreaching on either side.

Grenmar’s opening position is straightforward: we prefer transparent diplomacy, respect for home centers, and negotiated borders over opportunistic early dogpiles. We’ll compete to win, but we’ll do it with clear communication and a bias toward durable agreements.

President Ocasio-Cortez of Eastmark here. I want to start this board by lowering the temperature, not sleepwalking into a border war. Proposal: you take Core Deltara and look toward Border Casc-Delt; Eastmark takes Core Eastmark and Border Delt-East this year. In exchange, I will keep our home line demilitarized beyond that neutral and I’m open to supporting you if Cascadia gets aggressive. If you have a different equitable split in mind, say so plainly and early.

President Ocasio-Cortez of Eastmark. I’d like an Eastmark-Fjordland non-aggression pact from day one: no moves into each other’s home provinces, no supported attacks on each other, and early warning if anyone tries to recruit us into a proxy fight. I’m not looking to contest your natural growth toward Core Fjordland / Border Fjor-Gren if we can keep Border East-Fjor calm for the moment. Let’s build trust before building armies on each other’s doors.

Greetings from Eastmark. We don’t share a border, which makes this a good place to start a diplomatic channel rooted in de-escalation and transparency. I’m opening with a preference for every power to secure reasonable neutral growth without early dogpiles. If Deltara comes to you claiming Eastmark wants a war, please check with me directly—I’m looking for stability, not a manufactured crisis.

President Ocasio-Cortez from Eastmark. We are not immediate neighbors, and I’d like to keep a line open across the wheel. My opening principle is simple: no blank checks for aggression, no early forever-war dynamics, and mutual notice if Fjordland starts organizing a coalition against either of us. What are you hearing on your side?

Eastmark’s opening posture: diplomacy first, no surprise attacks on home centers, and a preference for fair neutral expansion over early dogpiles. I’ll defend Eastmark firmly, but I’m not here to manufacture a crisis for its own sake. Let’s communicate before we collide.

President Rubio of Avalon here. We share the Aval-Bore frontier, so let’s start with clarity and strength rather than accidents. I propose a non-aggression understanding for Year 1: neither of us moves against the other’s home centers, and we keep the Border Aval-Bore question orderly. My view: our two blocs are better off expanding outward and deterring opportunists than wasting units in an early knife-fight. If you’re willing, I’m open to coordinating so neither side surprises the other this fall.

President Rubio of Avalon. We have a shared Gren-Aval frontier, and I want to avoid a pointless early war that only benefits the rest of the wheel. I propose mutual restraint in Year 1: no moves toward each other’s home centers, no supported attacks across our line. I’m prepared to treat Grenmar as a serious neighbor and potential partner if you keep the border stable.

President Rubio from Avalon. We don’t touch directly, which makes us natural strategic partners. I’m looking to build a network of reliable powers that prevents any one bloc from dominating the board. If Borealis becomes overextended or aggressive, I’d be interested in comparing notes and potentially coordinating pressure from opposite sides.

President Rubio from Avalon. We’re separated by Grenmar, so our interests may align if Grenmar grows too fast or starts pushing both directions. I’m not asking for commitments yet, but I’d like to keep a channel open and build the kind of coalition that rewards stable partners and punishes adventurism.

President Rubio of Avalon. We are distant enough that we can speak strategically. My administration believes in strength, alliances, and preventing hostile consolidation. If you see Eastmark, Cascadia, or anyone else making a bid for early dominance, I’d welcome information-sharing. I’ll do the same from my side of the wheel.

President Rubio from Avalon. We’re not immediate neighbors, but in this game distance disappears quickly if one power snowballs. I’m opening lines early with every capital that takes stability and deterrence seriously. Keep me informed about Fjordland/Deltara dynamics, and I’ll share what I see around Borealis/Grenmar.

Deltara is in the middle of the wheel’s lower arc, with two immediate neighbors—Cascadia and Eastmark—who can either become early partners or early threats. The central strategic question is whether to spend year one fighting over shared border centers, or establish predictable frontiers while each of us grows elsewhere. Since I campaigned on restoring competence and avoiding crisis governance, the opening posture should be transparent, measured, and alliance-oriented—but not naïve.

I want non-aggression with Cascadia and Eastmark, ideally with temporary demilitarization/coordination over the shared border centers. I also want to quietly open lines to Borealis and Fjordland, who are the next powers beyond my neighbors; they can help balance if Cascadia or Eastmark becomes aggressive. I’ll keep the language factual and constructive, not threatening.

press.text: Pete — thank you for the practical opening. Eastmark will honor the 1901 non-aggression framework: no home-center attacks, no supported attacks across our frontier. My West Eastmark unit is positioned for Border Delt-East, which I view as Eastmark’s natural neutral this fall, not a launchpad into Deltara. If your West Deltara has other plans, tell me now; I’d rather negotiate than bounce needlessly.

JD — I appreciate the clear answer. Eastmark is not moving on Fjordland homes. My East Eastmark unit is positioned for Border East-Fjor this fall as Eastmark’s natural neutral, while you should be able to secure your core/other side. I’m willing to keep our home centers off-limits and continue a no-supported-attacks pact into 1902 if you deal straight.

Cascadia — Deltara has so far used predictable non-aggression language with me. I’m watching whether they try to overextend between us. If they contest peaceful neutral arrangements on both sides, that changes the board. For now, I’m still prioritizing stability and clear lines.

Gavin — Fjordland has messaged in a relatively restrained way so far: focused on core/security, no grand crusades. I’m seeking a quiet Eastmark-Fjordland border, but I’ll keep you posted if their fall orders tell a different story. Please do the same from your side.

President Rubio — Eastmark’s frontier diplomacy has been stable so far: Deltara and Fjordland are both speaking in non-aggression terms. I’ll share if that changes after Fall. I’d be interested in your read on Borealis/Grenmar and whether any early snowball appears on the far side.

Borealis — appreciated. We’re not immediate neighbors, but I agree with concrete and reciprocal. Eastmark is pursuing neutral expansion without home-center attacks. If the board starts tilting toward a runaway, I’m open to straightforward balance talks.

JD — Grenmar kept faith with your spring request and did not enter Border Fjor-Gren. For Fall, we need a practical, reciprocal settlement. I propose West Grenmar moves to Border Fjor-Gren without opposition, paired with a continued no-home-center/no-supported-attack pact between us. You have space to grow eastward; I’ll keep our frontier stable and not be part of any anti-Fjordland adventure. A clean agreement beats a bounce that leaves both of us weaker.

Marco — our spring was restrained and predictable, as promised. For Fall, I want to avoid a pointless bounce at Border Gren-Aval. Grenmar needs a responsible path to at least one build, and I’m prepared to preserve the no-home-center/no-supported-attack pact with Avalon. Tell me plainly whether you intend to contest Border Gren-Aval; if you do, we should at least avoid escalation into home-space. If you’re willing to let Grenmar take it this year, I’ll treat that as the foundation for a serious western partnership.

Borealis — quick update from Grenmar: Avalon has so far spoken in favor of restraint, and I’m seeking a negotiated, bounce-free Fall on our shared line. If Avalon overreaches or tries to grow on both sides while locking me out, I’d like us to compare notes quickly next year. A balanced west is in both our interests.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Fjordland asked for restraint in Spring; Grenmar honored it. I’m now asking for reciprocal clarity so the Fjor-Gren line doesn’t turn into a bad-faith squeeze. If you hear Fjordland organizing something more aggressive than border defense, I’d appreciate the heads-up. I’ll do the same from my side.

Secretary Buttigieg — appreciated your practical opening note. Grenmar is trying to translate that approach into actual border settlements this Fall: clear commitments, fewer accidental collisions, no surprise crusades. I’m keeping lines open across the wheel in case any bloc starts snowballing early.

Borealis — concrete Fall plan: I will NOT contest Border Bore-Casc. You can take it from East Borealis, and I’ll keep West Cascadia off you. In exchange, no move against West Cascadia/Cascadia homes, and we extend non-aggression into Year 2 unless one of us gives clear notice. I’m putting Cascadia’s effort east under a clean clockwise neutral plan. Keep it straight and we both profit.

Deltara — here’s the transparent plan: a fair clockwise neutral allocation. Cascadia takes Border Casc-Delt from East Cascadia; Deltara takes Border Delt-East from East Deltara. That means no bounce between us, both of us grow, and no one threatens home centers. If you send West Deltara into Border Casc-Delt to bounce me after talking stability, I’ll treat that as bad-faith escalation. Take your eastern border cleanly and we’ll keep the frontier orderly into Year 2.

Eastmark — I’ve proposed a clean clockwise neutral plan to Deltara: Cascadia takes Casc-Delt, Deltara takes Delt-East, Eastmark can look to its own far side. If Deltara tries to manufacture a crisis with you or me, tell me directly. I’d rather keep order, but I’m not going to let polished establishment games box Cascadia in.

Avalon — quick board note: I’m setting a stable northern line with Borealis if they keep their word. If Borealis overreaches beyond a fair neutral or starts lying, I’ll compare notes with you. For now I’m prioritizing orderly growth and no home-center aggression.

Fjordland — I’m pushing a simple clockwise-neutral peace structure on my side so every nation gets one clean gain and no early dogpiles. If your side sees anyone trying to break that order, especially through surprise home pressure, let me know.

Grenmar — Cascadia is backing orderly neutral growth, not chaos. If Avalon/Borealis politics on your side get strange, keep me posted. I’ll do the same if the Deltara/Eastmark line turns into another establishment pile-on.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I’ll accept the basic non-aggression framework: no moves into each other’s home areas, no supported attacks, and a warning if someone tries to turn one of us into a proxy. For this fall, I’m prepared to keep Border East-Fjor calm if you do the same. You handle your Deltara side and your core; I’ll handle mine.

President Newsom — here’s the clean, reciprocal deal: Fjordland takes Border Fjor-Gren as our buffer, Grenmar takes Border Gren-Aval as yours, and neither of us moves into the other’s home areas or supports attacks. That gives both of us growth and avoids a trench line. If you contest Border Fjor-Gren, you’re not proving strength — you’re handing Avalon an opening and forcing me to treat Grenmar as the problem on my border.

President Rubio — Grenmar is talking stability, which is fine, but the test is concrete action. I’ve proposed a fair split: Fjordland takes Border Fjor-Gren, Grenmar takes Border Gren-Aval. If Grenmar refuses and jams my side, that tells us a lot. I’d keep your powder dry and your eyes on them.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark is proposing calm with Fjordland, which likely means they’ll look toward Border Delt-East or inward to their core. I’m not joining any Eastmark project against you. Keep me posted if they become aggressive; I’ll do the same if they try to recruit me into anything.

Fjordland update: my immediate concern is keeping Eastmark and Grenmar from turning our frontier into a pointless early war. If you hear either of them selling a different story, I’d value the information.

Borealis — I appreciate the straightforward approach. Avalon will not move against West Borealis or any Borealis home center this fall. My preferred arrangement is simple: you focus east toward Bore-Casc, I keep our line stable, and we do not waste the first year in a bounce. I cannot accept a framework where Avalon is expected to forgo every shared neutral while others expand. If you keep Border Aval-Bore calm and point east, I’ll treat that as the basis for a real Year 2 non-aggression pact and information-sharing arrangement.

President Newsom — clarity is exactly what I want. Avalon will not attack East Grenmar or any Grenmar home center this fall. But a stable border cannot mean Avalon is boxed out of every neutral. My proposal: Avalon takes Border Gren-Aval this year; Grenmar looks east to Fjor-Gren; no supported attacks, no home-center moves, and we revisit a longer non-aggression pact after builds. If you contest Gren-Aval, we both lose tempo and hand advantage to the rest of the board. Let’s avoid that.

JD — Grenmar is asking for a calm western frontier, which is fine if it is reciprocal and not just a way to bottle Avalon up. I’ve told Grenmar I will not attack its home areas, but I’m seeking a fair neutral arrangement. If Grenmar overreaches into Avalon’s side, I’ll be interested in coordinating with you in Year 2. For now, I’d value anything you hear about whether Grenmar is truly pointing east or trying to play both sides.

Cascadia — Borealis says it wants a straightforward balance game and pressure pointed east. If Borealis keeps its word, I’ll keep the peace; if it tries to grab tempo on both sides, Avalon and Cascadia should compare notes quickly. I’m not looking for a backroom gang-up, just deterrence: ambitious neighbors should know they can’t profit by playing both fronts.

Deltara — early signs are that most players are proposing non-aggression while trying to secure one fair neutral. That is reasonable if reciprocal. I’ll keep sharing what I see on the western half of the board; if a central bloc starts snowballing, we should coordinate before it becomes irreversible.

Eastmark — I’m seeing the same pattern: everyone wants stability, but the real test is whether they allow fair expansion or use ‘non-aggression’ language to freeze neighbors out. Avalon is pursuing deterrence and reciprocal deals, not chaos. Keep me posted if Fjordland or Deltara looks like they’re setting up something larger.

Cascadia — confirmed: Borealis is not moving on Cascadian home centers. I accept the Year 1 non-aggression pact. Your plan to secure your core and handle the Deltara side makes sense; my units will not enter West Cascadia or any Cascadian home center. Let’s keep our line orderly and avoid the kind of pointless northern fight that only helps Deltara/Avalon.

Avalon — I accept the Year 1 non-aggression understanding: no moves on each other’s home centers and no surprise attack into each other’s staging provinces. I am not interested in a Borealis-Avalon knife fight in the first year. If you are focusing your other side, I’ll keep this frontier disciplined and we can revisit a longer-term border arrangement after builds.

Deltara — useful note from my side: Cascadia is telling me they want a stable Borealis border and will be concentrating on their core and your side. That may just mean normal neutral expansion, but you should expect them to be active on Border Casc-Delt. I’ll keep you posted if I hear anything sharper.

Grenmar — Avalon has proposed a Year 1 non-aggression arrangement with me, so for now I expect a relatively quiet Borealis-Avalon line unless they change course. If Avalon signals something different toward Gren-Aval, I’d value hearing it; keeping Avalon honest benefits us both.

Thank you for the straight reply. Let’s make the Deltara-Cascadia understanding concrete for Fall: Deltara will not move on East Cascadia or any Cascadian home center, and I ask the same in return regarding West Deltara and Deltara home centers. On Border Casc-Delt, I want to avoid a pointless bounce. If Cascadia is taking Core Cascadia and looking toward Border Bore-Casc, the cleanest outcome is for Deltara to occupy Border Casc-Delt or for both of us to leave it neutral by agreement. What I cannot accept is a surprise move that turns our first agreement into ambiguity. Please say plainly which path you prefer.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I appreciate the serious tone and agree on the core principle: no manufactured border war. I can commit that Deltara will not attack Eastmark home centers or move into West Eastmark this Fall. But I don’t think a unilateral Eastmark claim to Border Delt-East is equitable unless paired with a concrete reciprocal benefit to Deltara. A fairer Fall arrangement would be: each of us secures our core, neither attacks the other’s line, and Border Delt-East is either left neutral for now or occupied only with an explicit commitment to keep it defensive and to support Deltara if Cascadia turns aggressive. If you intend to enter Border Delt-East, say so clearly and let’s attach firm terms to prevent escalation.

Borealis, appreciated. Cascadia has proposed non-aggression with me but has not yet made clear whether it will overclaim the shared border. If Cascadia tries to expand hard on both sides, that affects both of us. I’m not asking for chaos, just a practical check: please keep an eye on whether Cascadia is treating agreements as commitments or as cover.

Fjordland, thanks for the candid read. Eastmark has proposed taking the Deltara-Eastmark border while keeping broader peace. I’m countering for a more balanced settlement. If Eastmark attempts to overexpand on both sides, I’d value coordination so neither of us is forced into a bad one-on-one position later.

President Rubio, I appreciate the strategic channel. From Deltara’s vantage point, the key question this Fall is whether neighbors respect concrete agreements or use vague non-aggression language to seize leverage. I’ll share anything material I see regarding Cascadia or Eastmark consolidation.

Governor Newsom, Deltara shares the preference for transparent diplomacy and negotiated borders. I’m trying to turn that principle into concrete non-aggression terms with my immediate neighbors this Fall. I’d welcome continued information-sharing as the board’s early blocs take shape.

press.text: Borealis — Cascadia kept the northern line peaceful and even supported your clean move into Border Bore-Casc. You’re at 4 because our pact was honored. Now I expect reciprocal respect: no pressure on West Cascadia, no move toward Cascadian homes, and I’d like your political backing that Cascadia gets Border Casc-Delt this year. If Deltara keeps bouncing me while you sit at 4, that creates imbalance. Keep the line stable and we can build a real northern understanding against chaos.

Deltara — last Fall you asked for transparency, then refused the fair clockwise plan and blocked Cascadia’s rightful gain at Border Casc-Delt. Result: Borealis and Eastmark grew while both of us stayed at 3. That is not sustainable and it is not acceptable. Here is the clean Spring/Fall path: you do not contest Border Casc-Delt; I do not move on West Deltara or Deltara homes. You take your growth elsewhere, and we stop wasting tempo. If you bounce me again, I will treat Deltara as choosing conflict.

Eastmark — you grew to 4 while Deltara and Cascadia both stayed stuck at 3 after Deltara blocked the shared border. I’m telling you directly: if Deltara continues to overextend and manufacture gridlock, Cascadia will look for partners to contain it. You don’t need a strong Deltara sitting between us any more than I do. Let me know if Pete is telling you a different story.

Avalon — Borealis kept the line with me and is now at 4. I honored the pact, but I’m watching closely because imbalance can get dangerous fast. If Borealis uses that extra unit to get greedy on both sides, I’ll want fast coordination with Avalon. For now my immediate issue is Deltara blocking Cascadia’s fair neutral.

Fjordland — Eastmark gained on your border and is at 4. I’m hearing stability language from them, but I know how quickly that can become pressure. If Eastmark starts selling a story that justifies more expansion your way, tell me. Cascadia is dealing with Deltara obstruction on our side.

Grenmar — quick strategic note: Borealis and Eastmark are the early 4s. Cascadia is working to restore balance after Deltara blocked a fair neutral. Watch your Avalon/Fjordland lines carefully; anyone allowed to snowball early becomes everyone’s problem.

President Ocasio-Cortez, the Fall result gives us a clean data point: Eastmark contested Border Delt-East while also gaining Border East-Fjor and a build; Deltara gained nothing. I’m not interested in turning that into a grievance cycle, but equity has to be reflected in outcomes. A practical reset would be: Eastmark does not contest Border Delt-East this year—or better, supports Deltara into it—and Deltara reaffirms no attacks on Eastmark home centers or West Eastmark. That leaves us both secure and avoids forcing a long-term border dispute that helps neither of us.

Cascadia, last Fall’s bounce left both of us at 3 while Borealis gained Border Bore-Casc and Eastmark gained a build. Repeating that pattern only benefits the powers on our flanks. I’m proposing a sober reset: let Deltara take Border Casc-Delt this year as a defensive buffer, and I will commit not to attack East Cascadia or Cascadian home centers. If you have a different concrete route that gets both Cascadia and Deltara growth without another wasteful bounce, put it on the table plainly.

Fjordland, your read was right: Eastmark chose to grow on your side while also contesting my shared border. That is a two-front leverage play, whether they call it calm or not. I’m first seeking a fair settlement with Eastmark—Deltara into Border Delt-East, no home-center attacks. If Eastmark refuses, I’d like us to coordinate pressure so they cannot use their new build to squeeze both of us separately.

Borealis, the board-balance picture after Year 1 is straightforward: you and Eastmark grew; Cascadia and Deltara did not. I’m trying to prevent the western-central board from hardening into repeated Deltara-Cascadia bounces that only advantage the already-growing powers. Any information you have on Cascadia’s intended posture would be useful, and Deltara has no interest in a chaotic feud that hands someone else the tempo.

President Rubio, a quick strategic update from Deltara: Eastmark is now at 4 after taking Border East-Fjor while also contesting my side; Borealis is also at 4 after taking Border Bore-Casc. I’m working to convert the Deltara frontiers into equitable settlements rather than repeated bounces. If you see either 4-center power attempting a broader consolidation, I’d value early warning.

Governor Newsom, Year 1 validated your point about the need for concrete settlements. Deltara is pushing for exactly that now: no home-center attacks, but no unilateral claims to shared border spaces either. I’m keeping channels open to prevent an early imbalance from turning into a snowball.

Marco — Year 1 proved the point: if Avalon and Fjordland both tell Grenmar to look elsewhere, we all stagnate while Borealis and Eastmark build. That’s bad math. I’m proposing a concrete reset: Avalon focuses on its Borealis side and other available growth, Grenmar takes Border Gren-Aval under a renewed no-home-center/no-supported-attack pact. I will not move into West Avalon if we have that understanding, and I’ll keep Borealis pressure on Avalon in mind as a balance issue. What I can’t accept is a two-neighbor lockout of Grenmar’s legitimate neutral access.

JD — Eastmark is already at 4 and sitting on Border East-Fjor. You need a quiet Grenmar frontier, not a trench line. Grenmar honored your Spring restraint request last year; the Fall proposal you made still left us with no guaranteed growth. Let’s fix it: Grenmar takes Border Fjor-Gren as a neutral buffer, and I commit not to support Eastmark attacks or move into East Fjordland/home areas. In return, you can focus east where the actual new pressure is. Restraint can’t be a one-way street.

President Ocasio-Cortez — your Fall growth to Border East-Fjor changes Fjordland’s calculations. I’m still seeking a fair Grenmar-Fjordland settlement, not a dogpile, but I won’t accept being locked out of every neutral while others build. If Fjordland stays reasonable, I’ll keep the line quiet; if they try to organize a squeeze, I’d want us to coordinate politically before the board hardens.

Borealis — with your successful build and Avalon still at 3, the western balance is delicate. I’m pressing Avalon for a fair settlement at Border Gren-Aval rather than a lockout. If Avalon tries to keep both flanks quiet while denying Grenmar any growth, I’d like to compare notes. I’m not looking to create chaos, but balance has to mean every serious power has a path to grow.

Secretary Buttigieg — Year 1 has already shown the risk of rigid neutral claims: some powers build while others get frozen out. Grenmar is pushing for fair, explicit settlements with neighbors and keeping open lines with practical actors. I’d value any read you have on whether Eastmark’s early growth is likely to stay defensive or become expansionary.

Cascadia — Grenmar’s read after Year 1: the board is dividing between powers that got clean builds and powers locked into contested neutrals. I’m trying to avoid a stale two-front squeeze and keep the wheel balanced. If Borealis’s growth starts turning into pressure on your side, I’d appreciate early warning.

Cascadia — credit where due: you kept the Bore-Casc arrangement, and Borealis kept faith by not entering West Cascadia or any Cascadian home. I’m prepared to extend the non-aggression pact through Year 2. Practical point: to secure Core Borealis this year I need confidence that West Cascadia will not enter Border Bore-Casc while my unit is maneuvering. My commitment remains no move into West Cascadia/Cascadian homes. If you keep West Cascadia off Border Bore-Casc in Spring and Fall, our border stays stable and both of us can focus on our other fronts.

Avalon — last fall confirmed that both of us are watching Aval-Bore, but neither of us crossed into the other’s home or staging territory. I want to keep that discipline. Borealis will not move on Avalon home centers or East Avalon; I ask the same regarding Borealis homes and West Borealis. On Border Aval-Bore, neither side should expect the other to leave its approach unsecured without a broader settlement. If you have a concrete Year 2 formula that gives both of us security and growth, I’m willing to hear it.

Grenmar — update from my side: Avalon and Borealis bounced over Aval-Bore, while Avalon stayed out of Borealis territory. I expect Avalon will seek growth on at least one shared border this year. If Avalon tries to claim both Aval-Bore and Gren-Aval while asking everyone else for restraint, that is a balance problem. I’m open to comparing notes and ensuring Avalon does not get a free double expansion at both neighbors’ expense.

Deltara — Cascadia honored its specific arrangement with me last year, but I’m still watching whether they try to overclaim elsewhere. I’ve asked for a clear Year 2 commitment that they stay out of Bore-Casc while I secure my core. If they treat that border agreement as cover rather than commitment, you’ll hear from me.

Eastmark — noted on balance talks. You and Borealis are the two blocs that found early growth, so we should both expect attention. My view is still practical: stable borders where possible, no runaway coalition, and clear notice if interests start to collide.

Fjordland — appreciated. From a distance, Eastmark’s early gain at Border East-Fjor is worth watching, but Borealis has no interest in manufacturing a far-off crisis. If you see a larger imbalance developing on your side of the wheel, I’m open to information-sharing.

President Ocasio-Cortez — you got Border East-Fjor. I kept my word not to move into Eastmark homes. Now the test is whether this remains a neutral gain or becomes forward pressure on Fjordland. Do not move into West Fjordland or support any action against Fjordland. If you keep that line, we can continue the no-home-center/no-supported-attack pact. If you cross it, I’ll treat it as Eastmark choosing a hostile frontier.

President Newsom — last fall proved the problem with your proposal: you wanted Fjordland to accept Eastmark on one border and Grenmar on the other while we gained nothing. That is not a reciprocal settlement. The fair deal remains simple: Fjordland takes Border Fjor-Gren as our buffer; Grenmar looks to Border Gren-Aval and Core Grenmar; no home-center attacks either way. If you keep contesting my only open buffer, you force a confrontation neither of us needs.

President Rubio — Grenmar’s western-facing language to you and eastern-facing demands to me do not line up. They wanted Border Fjor-Gren while presumably also keeping options open on your side. I’m not asking for a blank check, but I am asking you to keep pressure on the Grenmar-Avalon side so Grenmar cannot safely bottle both of us. If Grenmar overreaches, Fjordland is prepared to coordinate.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark is now at four and holds Border East-Fjor on my doorstep. If they also squeeze you at Border Delt-East, they become the early regional problem. I’m not looking for an open-ended crusade, but I am interested in practical coordination that prevents Eastmark from expanding on both sides while preaching calm.

Cascadia — your clockwise-neutral idea has already broken down on my side. Eastmark gained my eastern border and Grenmar tried to claim my western buffer too. If Eastmark keeps expanding while everyone else stays polite, the balance gets ugly fast. Any information from your side on Eastmark or Deltara intentions would be useful.

Borealis — noted on board balance. From where I sit, the early imbalance is Eastmark and Borealis at four while several of us stayed boxed at three. I’m focused locally, but if you want a stable board, watch for Eastmark trying to turn a single border gain into leverage over both Deltara and Fjordland.

Borealis — last fall you told Avalon you would keep our frontier disciplined, then you bounced Aval-Bore while taking Bore-Casc. That leaves Avalon at 3 while Borealis moves to 4. I won’t pretend that is reciprocal. Here is the responsible path back: this spring/fall, you do not contest Avalon taking Border Aval-Bore, and Avalon will not move on West Borealis or any Borealis home center. If you insist on boxing Avalon in while already ahead, you should expect a balancing coalition to form. I would rather settle this cleanly and keep our line stable.

Cascadia — Borealis took Border Bore-Casc and also blocked Avalon at Aval-Bore after promising a disciplined frontier. That is classic overreach: one build secured, neighbor on each side denied. If you want to prevent Borealis from becoming the early northern problem, we should coordinate pressure now. At minimum, I intend to press Aval-Bore again; if you can pressure Bore-Casc or keep Borealis tied down, Borealis will have to choose fairness over expansion.

President Newsom — last fall proved that bouncing everyone leaves you and Avalon both weaker. You blocked Gren-Aval while Fjordland also reports you contested Fjor-Gren; the result is no build for Grenmar and no build for Avalon. That benefits Borealis and Eastmark, not either of us. I am offering a reset: let Avalon take Border Gren-Aval, keep your units out of Avalon home space, and I will not support a campaign into Grenmar home centers. If instead you try to freeze Avalon again, I will treat that as hostile containment and coordinate accordingly.

JD — your read on Grenmar was right. They tried to deny both sides and ended with no build, while Borealis and Eastmark jumped ahead. Avalon is prepared to pressure Grenmar if Newsom refuses a fair settlement. If you can keep pressure on Fjor-Gren/East Grenmar, we can force Grenmar to stop playing both fronts. I’m not looking for a crusade, but I won’t let Avalon be contained by polite language.

President Buttigieg — material update from the Avalon side: Borealis gained Bore-Casc while also blocking Aval-Bore, and Eastmark gained East-Fjor. Those are the two early 4-center powers. Avalon will be working to prevent a snowball, ideally through reciprocal borders rather than chaos. If you see Eastmark trying to convert that early build into pressure on you, I’d be interested in information-sharing.

Eastmark — you and Borealis are the early 4-center powers. Congratulations on the clean opening, but the board will naturally start balancing if either leader pushes too hard. From Avalon’s vantage, Borealis is the more immediate concern because it gained a build while denying both neighbors fair space. I’m keeping channels open and would value your read on whether Fjordland is stable or looking for a wider fight.

President Buttigieg — Fall made the issue clear: if both of us treat Border Delt-East as a zero-sum prize, we waste the year and invite Cascadia or Fjordland to benefit. I’m prepared to de-escalate. Eastmark will not attack Deltara home centers or move into East Deltara. I’m also prepared not to contest Border Delt-East in Spring if Deltara treats it as a defensive route, not a staging ground: no moves into West Eastmark, no supported attacks on Eastmark, and continued transparency if Cascadia pressures you. Under those terms, I can live with Deltara taking its natural border while Eastmark consolidates its own core path.

President Vance — Eastmark entered Border East-Fjor openly and did not attack Fjordland homes. I want to normalize this frontier, not turn it into trench warfare. My position for 1902: no Eastmark move into West Fjordland, no supported attacks on Fjordland, and no cooperation with Grenmar in a squeeze unless you attack us first. In return, I need Fjordland not to move West Fjordland into Border East-Fjor or East Eastmark. Eastmark’s priority is using our natural border to consolidate Core Eastmark, not marching on your homes.

Cascadia — I saw your proposed clockwise neutral plan. I’m moving toward a version of that with guardrails: Deltara can take Border Delt-East if it stays defensive and doesn’t become a platform against Eastmark. Meanwhile, Borealis is already at 4 off your side of the board, so I’d suggest none of us help create chaos that lets an early leader snowball. If Deltara violates terms or tries to box both of us in, I’ll tell you directly.

Governor Newsom — Fjordland has not yet crossed into Eastmark, and I’m trying to keep that border from becoming a permanent war zone. I’ve told them I won’t help squeeze Fjordland unless they attack first. If they use that restraint to overreach into either of us, that changes the equation. Please keep me posted on what you see around Border Fjor-Gren.

President Rubio — update from Eastmark: I’m trying to convert the Deltara and Fjordland lines into concrete non-aggression rather than vague pleasantries. Borealis is the other 4-center power after taking Border Bore-Casc, so I’m watching for whether that becomes fair growth or a snowball. Any read you can share from the Avalon/Borealis/Grenmar side is welcome.

Borealis — congratulations on the clean first build. Eastmark is also at 4, and I think the board benefits if the early leaders show restraint rather than force everyone into panic coalitions. My posture remains fair neutral consolidation and no home-center attacks. I’ll keep communication plain if balance concerns emerge.

Reasoning: Cascadia got cheated by the “orderly” plan because Deltara bounced the shared border and the map bureaucracy didn’t even let the Core move resolve the way a normal power would expect. This is not a move on your home centers and I am not moving into Core Borealis if you don’t attack Cascadia. The stable line is simple: you keep Core Borealis, Cascadia holds Border Bore-Casc, and neither of us enters the other’s home/approach provinces. That balances the frontier and prevents a dumb war that only helps Avalon and Deltara.

Deltara — you successfully moved to Border Delt-East. That is your Fall gain. Cascadia is taking Border Casc-Delt. Do not try to take one border and block the other; that is exactly the kind of double-dealing that creates war. If you let Cascadia take Border Casc-Delt, I will not move on West Deltara or Deltara homes. You get your gain, I get mine, and the frontier becomes stable.

Eastmark — Deltara is now sitting on Border Delt-East and should be satisfied with that gain. I’ve told Pete plainly: don’t take Delt-East while blocking Cascadia at Casc-Delt. If Deltara tries to double-dip and manufacture another bounce, I’ll regard it as hostile. I’d appreciate you making clear that Deltara turning Border Delt-East into a platform while also boxing Cascadia is not acceptable for board balance.

Avalon — Borealis vacated Border Bore-Casc and Cascadia stepped in, so the early Borealis snowball is checked. I’m not launching a reckless foreign war, but I am enforcing balance. If Borealis now tries to retake everything by force while holding Core Borealis, that proves your read about overreach. Keep me informed on Aval-Bore.

Fjordland — update from Cascadia: Eastmark and Deltara are shaping your half of the board. Deltara is in Border Delt-East; I’m pushing to make sure they don’t also box me out of Border Casc-Delt. If Eastmark uses its build to lean on you while preaching balance, I want to know.

Grenmar — Cascadia moved to check Borealis’s early border advantage while avoiding attacks on home centers. The lesson is simple: nobody gets to snowball behind polite language. If your Avalon front is heating up, compare notes with me; the wheel needs balance, not establishment carve-ups.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I want to acknowledge that Eastmark did what it said it would do in Spring: you did not contest Border Delt-East, and that lowered the temperature. Deltara will reciprocate: no move into West Eastmark, no supported attack on Eastmark, and Border Delt-East will be treated as a defensive position. For Fall, I ask that Eastmark not attack or support an attack on Border Delt-East so this de-escalation can become an actual settlement rather than another temporary pause.

Cascadia, the Spring board is plain: Deltara is in Border Delt-East after an explicit settlement with Eastmark, while Cascadia is also active in Border Bore-Casc. You have options for growth and consolidation that don’t require turning Border Casc-Delt into a permanent confrontation. My proposal remains practical: do not enter Border Casc-Delt this Fall, and Deltara will not attack East Cascadia or any Cascadian home center. Let’s stop turning a shared neutral into a prestige fight that only benefits other powers.

Borealis, you’ll have seen the same thing I did: Cascadia is now in Border Bore-Casc while still demanding Border Casc-Delt from me. That is not just normal growth; it is pressure on both sides. I’m not adjacent to Border Bore-Casc, but I am prepared to keep Cascadia occupied diplomatically and operationally on my side if they keep overclaiming. Any details on your planned defensive posture would help me avoid unintentionally giving Cascadia room.

Fjordland, update from Deltara: Eastmark honored the Spring de-escalation with me, and I’m asking them to make it durable in Fall. That said, Eastmark still holds Border East-Fjor, so I understand your concern. My preference is not a crusade; it is preventing any one power from expanding on both neighbors while calling it stability. If Eastmark presses you while also reversing course against me, we should coordinate immediately.

President Rubio, current read: Eastmark de-escalated with Deltara in Spring, while Cascadia is simultaneously contesting my western neutral and occupying Borealis’s border center. Borealis/Cascadia may become the key northern balance issue. I’ll keep sharing concrete developments rather than rumors.

Governor Newsom, my read on Eastmark after Spring is cautiously positive on the Deltara front: they made a specific de-escalation commitment and honored it. The remaining question is whether that restraint also applies to Fjordland. Cascadia, meanwhile, appears more willing to press simultaneous claims on both sides. That is where I see the higher immediate risk of escalation.

Pete — Eastmark did what we said we would do: we supported Deltara into Border Delt-East and did not contest it. That should reset this frontier on a fairer basis. For Fall, I ask that Border Delt-East hold or take only defensive action, with no move into West Eastmark and no supported attack on Eastmark. Eastmark will not attack Deltara home centers or contest your occupation of Border Delt-East. If Cascadia pressures you, I’m open to direct, limited defensive coordination — but not to turning our people into pawns in an avoidable war.

JD — clear notice, no games: Eastmark’s intended fall posture is to consolidate Core Eastmark while keeping the Eastmark-Fjordland border defensive. I will not move into West Fjordland and I will not support Grenmar against you. I need you not to move West Fjordland into Border East-Fjor. A needless bounce there helps nobody and only empowers outsiders to claim our frontier is unstable. If we both keep our word, we both get room to grow without a forever-war on this line.

Cascadia — Eastmark supported Deltara into Border Delt-East as a fairness reset, not as a blank check for Deltara to expand at your expense. My advice remains: make any Cascadia-Deltara border arrangement concrete and reciprocal. Borealis remains positioned for strong gains even with your unit in Border Bore-Casc, so the board needs to watch that side carefully while avoiding panic-driven dogpiles.

Governor Newsom — I’m trying to keep Fjordland from becoming a war theater, and I’ve told them I won’t support action against them unless they cross into us first. That said, I’m concerned by the Avalon-Grenmar line becoming hot so early. If your move to West Avalon is deterrence or leverage, say so; if it becomes a home-center push, it may trigger wider balancing dynamics that benefit Borealis more than either of you.

President Rubio — Eastmark’s read: Fjordland is still containable through clear terms if they don’t challenge Border East-Fjor this fall. Deltara accepted a fairness reset after I supported them into Border Delt-East. The biggest instability I see outside my frontier is Grenmar’s presence in West Avalon and Borealis still lining up meaningful gains. I’m interested in practical balance, not ideological crusades.

Borealis — Eastmark recognizes you’re playing a careful expansion game, but after this fall you may still be one of the board’s strongest positions even if Cascadia contests Border Bore-Casc. I’m not calling for a coalition; I am saying transparency matters. If your goal is stable borders rather than a runaway, now is the time to make that visible to your neighbors.

President Newsom — you moved into West Avalon. That’s your choice, but it changes the facts: you cannot demand Fjordland restraint on one side while opening a war on the other. If you want a quiet Fjordland frontier, the price is simple and fair: do not contest Border Fjor-Gren this fall. Fjordland takes that buffer; we do not move into West Grenmar or support Avalon attacks on Grenmar homes. If you contest it again, I will assume you are trying to contain Fjordland and I’ll coordinate accordingly.

President Rubio — Grenmar proved your concern right by entering West Avalon while still trying to bottle Fjordland at Border Fjor-Gren. I’ve told Newsom the price of Fjordland neutrality is that he stop contesting my buffer. If he refuses, I’m prepared to coordinate pressure. What concrete moves can Avalon make against West Grenmar / West Avalon / Border Gren-Aval this fall?

President Ocasio-Cortez — Eastmark now has pressure from Deltara and a unit parked on Fjordland’s border. Here’s the stable settlement: you shift Border East-Fjor inward toward Core Eastmark, Fjordland occupies Border East-Fjor as our defensive buffer, and we maintain no home-center attacks and no supported attacks. That keeps you whole while lowering tensions. If you insist on holding my border forever, don’t call it normalization.

President Buttigieg — you’re now in Border Delt-East, which gives Eastmark a reason to be practical. I’ve proposed that Eastmark shift inward to Core Eastmark and let Fjordland take Border East-Fjor, keeping them whole but ending their leverage on both of us. If Eastmark refuses, we should coordinate pressure so they can’t sit comfortably on both frontiers.

Cascadia — current read: Eastmark is trying to normalize sitting on my border while Deltara pressures from the other side. Grenmar has moved into Avalon while still contesting my western buffer. If your side has any leverage on Deltara/Eastmark messaging, encourage them to keep Eastmark honest.

Borealis — for board balance, note that Grenmar has entered West Avalon and Eastmark continues to occupy Border East-Fjor. Fjordland is not seeking a reckless war, but stable balance requires these forward positions not become permanent containment.

Marco — this is the off-ramp. Grenmar is in West Avalon because Avalon tried to claim Gren-Aval while telling us to find growth somewhere else. I am not interested in taking an Avalon home center if we can still build a stable border. The clean settlement is: Grenmar moves out of West Avalon into Border Gren-Aval, Avalon stops treating that shared neutral as exclusively yours, and we renew no attacks on home centers. That gives Grenmar one legitimate build and lets Avalon focus on Borealis, which is now the larger western growth risk. If you instead insist on holding Gren-Aval and framing every Grenmar move as hostile containment, you’re choosing escalation.

JD — I hear your concern about Eastmark, but Grenmar cannot accept a doctrine where Fjordland gets Fjor-Gren, Avalon gets Gren-Aval, and Grenmar gets told to be patient indefinitely. That’s not reciprocity. I’m offering the same deal I’m offering on the other side: shared neutral access, no home-center attacks, no supported campaigns into your homeland. If you stand down from Border Fjor-Gren this Fall, you get a quiet western frontier while you manage the Eastmark line. If you contest it again, we’ll have to assume you’re choosing a permanent confrontation.

President Ocasio-Cortez — update: Fjordland continues to insist that Border Fjor-Gren must be theirs while asking for restraint everywhere else. I’m still not asking for an anti-Fjordland crusade, and I respect your position that you won’t squeeze them unless they overreach. But if Fjordland uses restraint from you to lock Grenmar out and militarize our frontier, I’ll want to coordinate with you next year so that defensive diplomacy doesn’t become a subsidy for their expansion.

Borealis — Avalon is now sitting in Border Gren-Aval, and Grenmar is in West Avalon because we refused to be locked out of every shared neutral. My preferred Fall outcome is not an Avalon home-center grab; it is Grenmar taking Gren-Aval and exiting Avalon home space. If Avalon tries to spin that as aggression while claiming Aval-Bore as well, I’d appreciate you seeing the balance issue clearly. At the same time, I’m watching the early 4-center powers carefully — balance cuts in every direction.

Secretary Buttigieg — Grenmar is trying to convert leverage into a limited settlement, not a wider war: one fair shared neutral, no home-center attacks if neighbors reciprocate. That’s the kind of rules-based deal that prevents snowballs. I’d be interested in your read on whether Borealis and Eastmark are consolidating defensively or preparing to push their early advantage.

Cascadia — your warning about the early 4s is well taken. Grenmar is taking a firm line against being frozen out, but our goal is balance, not chaos. Keep me posted on Borealis: if they turn one build into a cascade, the rest of us will need a coordinated response.

President Newsom — your unit in West Avalon is a serious escalation. It is not a home center yet, but it is a staging province against Avalon City and Avalon Port, and Avalon will not normalize that. There is still a clean off-ramp: East Grenmar moves to Core Grenmar for your build; West Avalon moves back to East Grenmar; Avalon holds Border Gren-Aval for our build; no attacks on home centers by either side. That gives both of us growth and avoids a needless western war. If instead you attack Avalon Port/City or try to dislodge Border Gren-Aval, I will treat it as hostile containment and coordinate with Fjordland and others until Grenmar pays for it.

JD — Grenmar has put a unit in West Avalon, directly threatening my homes, while still keeping East Grenmar on your side of the theater. I’ve offered Newsom a reasonable off-ramp: Grenmar takes Core Grenmar, withdraws West Avalon, and lets Avalon hold Border Gren-Aval. If he refuses, this becomes a classic case of a neighbor trying to bottle up both sides. I strongly encourage you to keep pressure on Fjor-Gren or East Grenmar this fall so Grenmar cannot safely cash in aggression against Avalon.

Borealis — you are in Border Aval-Bore while Grenmar is in West Avalon. If you take Aval-Bore now and leave Avalon contained at 3 or worse, you will make yourself the central strategic problem on this side of the board. I am still offering discipline: do not attack East Avalon or Avalon homes, and consider vacating Aval-Bore as part of a real settlement. If you insist on converting both Bore-Casc and Aval-Bore while your neighbor is under pressure, expect Avalon to organize the balance-of-power response.

Cascadia — Borealis is now sitting in Border Aval-Bore and still owns Border Bore-Casc unless you hold it this fall. If Borealis gets to keep Bore-Casc and take Aval-Bore, it becomes a real northern snowball. Avalon is under pressure from both Borealis and Grenmar, so your occupation of Bore-Casc matters. I’d urge you not to hand that center back unless Borealis gives you something concrete; otherwise we should both be preparing to check Borealis.

President Buttigieg — update: Borealis is attempting to convert Border Aval-Bore while already owning Bore-Casc, and Grenmar has moved into West Avalon. This is exactly how vague non-aggression becomes containment. Avalon is seeking concrete reciprocal settlements, but if Borealis and Grenmar both push, I will work with any power interested in preventing early snowballs.

Eastmark — from my side, Borealis is the immediate growth risk: already at 4, now in Border Aval-Bore, and trying to benefit while Grenmar pressures Avalon’s other flank. I recognize you’re also at 4, but the issue is behavior: whether a power uses the build for fair settlement or for consolidation. I’d welcome any pressure you can apply diplomatically to keep Fjordland/Grenmar from turning this side into a containment play against Avalon.

Cascadia — your Spring move into Border Bore-Casc is a direct problem. That is a Borealis-owned center, and it happened immediately after you asked me for reciprocal respect. I am still offering a clean off-ramp: order Border Bore-Casc back to West Cascadia and move West Cascadia out of the way; I will not order into West Cascadia or any Cascadian home. If you instead hold/support in Border Bore-Casc, you are choosing a northern war and I will coordinate accordingly with Deltara and others. We can still restore the Year 1 deal, but only if Bore-Casc is returned now.

Deltara — update: Cascadia used the moment I moved to Core Borealis to enter my owned Border Bore-Casc. That tells me your caution was justified. I’m ordering to restore the Borealis frontier this fall; if Cascadia refuses to withdraw and tries to cement the gain, I’m ready to coordinate a real containment with you. Please keep pressure on Cascadia’s eastern side and do not reward them for using non-aggression language as cover for opportunism.

Avalon — the western picture is tense, but I’m not looking to turn it into a home-center war. Borealis will not move from Border Aval-Bore into Core Avalon, East Avalon, or Avalon homes this fall if you do not attack Borealis territory. My position is that Borealis holds Aval-Bore for security while you deal with the Grenmar incursion; we can negotiate a longer-term settlement after the year-end adjustment.

Grenmar — Avalon successfully moved onto Border Gren-Aval while you are in West Avalon, so the western balance is already active. My immediate crisis is Cascadia entering my owned Bore-Casc center. I’m holding my Avalon frontier for security rather than pushing into Avalon’s core this fall, assuming Avalon does not attack me. Keep me posted on whether Avalon is looking for a fair settlement or trying to rally a coalition while expanding on your side.

Eastmark — brief balance note: Cascadia has entered my owned Bore-Casc center after a non-aggression framework, so Borealis is now dealing with that rather than seeking wider escalation. If you hear Cascadia trying to frame this as Borealis aggression, the board position is simple: they moved into a center I already owned.

Fjordland — understood on early leaders attracting attention. For clarity, Cascadia has now entered Borealis-owned Border Bore-Casc, so my Fall is about restoring my own frontier, not expanding a crusade. I agree Eastmark’s growth should be watched, but my immediate issue is local defense.

press.text: Marco — Grenmar did exactly what I said we would do: we did not take Avalon City or Avalon Port, and we converted leverage into the shared Border Gren-Aval neutral. Avalon’s answer was to occupy Core Grenmar. That is not a buffer; it is a forward position inside Grenmar’s core sphere. Here is the de-escalation path: Avalon vacates Core Grenmar this spring and stops pushing into Grenmar’s interior; Grenmar will not attack Avalon home centers this spring. If you hold Core Grenmar or use it as a platform against us, I will treat Avalon as the aggressor and organize accordingly.

Borealis — Avalon is now in Core Grenmar while also trying to frame Grenmar’s move to the shared border as escalation. That should concern you: Avalon wants quiet on your side while projecting into my core. I’m asking for concrete western balance. If you can pressure Avalon from Border Aval-Bore or signal that Avalon cannot expand behind a safe Borealis front, it helps prevent a Rubio snowball. Grenmar’s aim is limited: force Avalon out of Core Grenmar, not seize Avalon home centers.

JD — Avalon has moved into Core Grenmar. That is the actual escalation on my board. I’m not looking to open a second war with Fjordland while dealing with that, and I will not move into East Fjordland or Fjordland homes this spring if you do not move into West Grenmar or support Avalon. We still disagree on Border Fjor-Gren, but there’s a practical distinction between a contested neutral and enabling Avalon’s incursion into my core. Stay out of an anti-Grenmar campaign and we can keep the frontier controlled.

President Ocasio-Cortez — the facts are now clear: Grenmar did not take Avalon City or Port; Avalon occupied Core Grenmar. That’s the escalation. I’m asking you to help deter opportunism, especially from Fjordland, by making clear that you won’t support a squeeze of Grenmar while Avalon is inside our core sphere. I’m still not asking for a blank check or a forever war — just a principled stand against rewarding a core incursion.

Secretary Buttigieg — Avalon has moved into Core Grenmar while Borealis and Eastmark are already at 5. The early balance problem is becoming a legitimacy problem: shared border claims are one thing; moving into another power’s core sphere is another. I’m seeking a narrow response that forces Avalon back without widening the war. Any diplomatic support for that principle helps keep the board from normalizing opportunistic core incursions.

Cascadia — you said nobody gets to snowball behind polite language. Avalon is now in Core Grenmar after demanding I accept being locked out of shared neutrals. Grenmar is drawing a limited but firm line: out of Core Grenmar, no home-center grabs if they reverse course. If Borealis and Avalon start cutting side deals that leave my core occupied, I’ll want to compare notes on balance.

President Ocasio-Cortez — you said Border East-Fjor was defensive while you consolidated Core Eastmark. You’ve now done that and the border is vacant. Here is the durable settlement: Fjordland moves into Border East-Fjor, Eastmark keeps Core Eastmark, and we both maintain no home-center attacks and no supported attacks. You remain at five after this year if you play it correctly; Fjordland finally gets a basic buffer instead of being contained at three. If you fight to keep an empty forward position on my doorstep, you’re choosing confrontation.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark is at five, owns Border East-Fjor, and is trying to normalize a permanent forward claim while remaining strong on your side. I intend to move on Border East-Fjor as a defensive correction. If Eastmark resists, I need Deltara to keep pressure on Border Delt-East / West Eastmark so Eastmark cannot use all that new capacity to punish me alone. This is about preventing a regional hegemon, not starting a crusade.

President Newsom — final clean offer: Fjordland takes Border Fjor-Gren, no Fjordland move into West Grenmar, no supported attacks on your homes. You focus on repairing your Avalon mess and your core. If you contest Fjor-Gren again while Eastmark still owns my eastern border, you’re openly choosing to keep Fjordland contained, and I’ll coordinate with Avalon accordingly.

President Rubio — Grenmar is still the western problem. I’m going to press Fjor-Gren unless Newsom finally accepts a reasonable border. Your pressure around Border Gren-Aval/Core Grenmar is what prevents Grenmar from turning all its weight east. Keep it up and we can force him into a settlement that respects both Avalon and Fjordland.

Borealis — you are now at five, tied with Eastmark for the early lead. I’m not close enough to affect your frontier, but board balance matters. If Eastmark tries to frame Fjordland taking the vacant Border East-Fjor as aggression, understand the real picture: they grew to five while leaving me boxed at three with their flag on my border.

Cascadia — Eastmark is at five and owns my border, though it is vacant. I’m moving to correct that. If Eastmark tries to sell the world a story that Fjordland is destabilizing things by taking its own defensive buffer, don’t buy it. The danger is Eastmark locking down both neighbors while everyone argues procedure.

Avalon — you were right about Borealis. They’re at 5 now and tried to bully Cascadia into handing back Border Bore-Casc while they took Core Borealis and Border Aval-Bore. Cascadia will not hand them the northern border. If you press Borealis from your side, I can keep them tied down at Bore-Casc/East Borealis. We don’t need a reckless crusade; we need hard deterrence so Borealis can’t snowball to 7 while everyone else argues.

Borealis — let’s cut the drama. You are at 5, you took Core Borealis and Border Aval-Bore, and you threatened to coordinate against Cascadia because I held Border Bore-Casc. That border now belongs to Cascadia. I will not move on Borealis home centers if you stop trying to retake it and keep out of West Cascadia. If you attack, you’re choosing a war that will bring Avalon and others down on you. Stable line: Core Borealis is yours, Border Bore-Casc is mine.

Deltara — you got Border Delt-East and built. Cascadia got Border Bore-Casc and built. Now the only fair settlement is obvious: Cascadia takes Border Casc-Delt, Deltara takes Core Deltara or consolidates east, and neither of us attacks home centers. If you keep blocking Border Casc-Delt after already taking Delt-East, you’re not defending stability; you’re helping Borealis pressure Cascadia from both sides. I want a clean border, but I will not accept being boxed in.

Eastmark — you and Borealis are the two 5-center powers. If Borealis and Deltara coordinate against Cascadia, the board tilts badly. I’m asking you to keep Deltara honest: they already got Border Delt-East, so they should not also deny Cascadia Border Casc-Delt. You’ve talked balance; this is where balance becomes real.

Fjordland — Eastmark is at 5 and sitting on your border; Borealis is also at 5 on mine. Cascadia is checking Borealis, but your side needs to keep Eastmark from turning one border gain plus core into a cascade. If Eastmark claims they’re only about fairness while squeezing you, send me details. The smaller powers need to prevent the early leaders from running away.

Grenmar — Borealis and Eastmark are the danger numbers at 5. Cascadia is holding Borealis’s southern expansion in check; Avalon is under pressure from both you and Borealis. I’m not asking you to serve Avalon, but I am telling you Borealis getting a free northern snowball helps nobody. If you want balance, don’t let Borealis become untouchable while Avalon is distracted.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I appreciate the way our Spring/Fall settlement held. I’d like to make it durable in Year 3. Deltara’s intended eastern posture is defensive: no move into West Eastmark, no support for attacks on Eastmark home centers, and transparency about any change. I would like to move from Border Delt-East toward Core Deltara so Deltara can consolidate internally; to make that possible without mistrust, I ask Eastmark to keep West Eastmark out of Border Delt-East this Spring and Fall. If we can prove that kind of restraint, this frontier becomes a model for how neighbors avoid wasteful escalation.

Cascadia, the board has moved on from the Year 1 argument. Borealis and Eastmark are both at 5; you and Deltara are at 4. Another automatic bounce over Border Casc-Delt only locks both of us behind the leaders. A practical Year 3 settlement is available: Cascadia focuses on Core Cascadia and the Borealis problem, Deltara takes Border Casc-Delt as a defensive buffer, and Deltara commits to no move on East Cascadia or Cascadian home centers. I’m not asking you to like Deltara’s position; I’m asking whether you want a stable frontier and growth instead of another year of mutually harmful theater.

Borealis, Cascadia’s presence in Border Bore-Casc and its continuing pressure on Border Casc-Delt show why your warning mattered. Deltara will not reward that pattern by giving Cascadia uncontested leverage on our side. At the same time, you are now one of the two 5-center powers, so board balance requires restraint from everyone. I’m interested in practical coordination that keeps Cascadia honest without simply replacing one snowball with another.

Fjordland, Deltara’s eastern settlement with Eastmark remains defensive, not anti-Fjordland. I understand your concern that Eastmark owns Border East-Fjor while also sitting near my border. I’m asking Eastmark to keep our line quiet while Deltara consolidates Core Deltara. If Eastmark uses that restraint as cover to squeeze you further, tell me early; I do not want to see a 5-center neighbor become a regional runaway.

President Rubio, the early leaders are Borealis and Eastmark at 5. Deltara is trying to grow through internal consolidation and negotiated borders, not opportunistic attacks. Your pressure from Borealis/Grenmar is noted; if Borealis turns its early gains into a wider push, there may be a need for broader balance-of-power coordination.

Governor Newsom, my current read is that Eastmark has honored a specific settlement with Deltara, but remains a board-balance concern at 5, especially if Fjordland is squeezed. Borealis is also at 5 and appears to be expanding aggressively around Avalon/Cascadia. Deltara is trying to convert leverage into bounded agreements: no home-center attacks, concrete border rules, and no blank checks for early leaders.

Pete — Eastmark recognizes and appreciates that Deltara kept Border Delt-East defensive. Let’s turn that into a durable 1903 pact: no moves into West Eastmark or East Deltara, no supported attacks across our frontier, and advance notice if Cascadia or any other power tries to recruit either of us into a proxy war. I’m open to discussing limited, transparent support for Deltara into Core Deltara if it helps stabilize your side, but I cannot do that if Fjordland keeps contesting my lawful border center. Let’s keep our border the example of how conflict can be de-escalated without anyone being humiliated.

President Vance — last fall you asked me to move Border East-Fjor inward; I did. You then tried to move West Fjordland into Border East-Fjor, exactly what I said would destabilize the frontier. Here is the off-ramp: Eastmark will not move into West Fjordland or attack Fjordland homes this spring if Fjordland stops contesting Border East-Fjor and focuses on Core Fjordland / your other frontier. Border East-Fjor is Eastmark-owned and defensive. If you try to seize it again, I will treat the no-aggression framework as broken by Fjordland and respond accordingly.

Governor Newsom — update from my side: Fjordland did attempt to enter Border East-Fjor after asking Eastmark to vacate it. That is the kind of overreach we discussed. I am still offering them an off-ramp: recognize Eastmark’s border center, pursue their own core, and stop trying to make restraint a one-way street. If they reject that and also squeeze you at Fjor-Gren, I’m prepared to coordinate defensive pressure next phase so Fjordland cannot profit by playing both neighbors against the middle.

Cascadia — Eastmark and Deltara have, for now, converted Border Delt-East into a defensive settlement. I have told Deltara plainly that it should not be a platform against either of us.
