press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez — Core Fjordland is now listed as an Eastmark center. That ends the fiction that this was temporary protection. You said you wouldn’t turn Fjordland into spoils, then you did exactly that. Here is the only acceptable off-ramp: vacate Core Fjordland this spring and make no move into Fjordland homes or West Fjordland. If you do, we can talk about a hard border and a non-aggression framework. If you hold it or use it to support pressure on Fjordland, I will organize every available neighbor against Eastmark’s occupation.

President Newsom — Eastmark converted Core Fjordland into an Eastmark center. That should concern you too: a six-center Eastmark sitting inside Fjordland’s core is not a buffer, it’s a platform. Fjordland will not attack Grenmar territory this spring if Grenmar supports Fjordland’s restoration of Core Fjordland and makes no move into East Fjordland or our homes. You said you did not want a partition. This is the test. Help restore Core Fjordland to Fjordland, and we maintain a controlled western frontier.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark crossed the line and converted Core Fjordland. The balance problem is no longer hypothetical. I need immediate pressure from your side: threaten or execute action against Core Eastmark / West Eastmark / Border Delt-East so Eastmark cannot commit every unit to holding my core. Fjordland’s case is narrow: restore Core Fjordland to its own people, no Eastmark occupation, no home-center escalation unless they force it.

Marco — we are the two three-center powers left while Borealis is at seven and Eastmark/Grenmar/Deltara sit at six. Eastmark just converted Core Fjordland the way Borealis sits in Core Avalon. This is the same problem in two theaters: bigger neighbors occupying the positions that decide whether smaller powers survive. Keep Grenmar and Borealis busy; I’m pressing for Core Fjordland’s restoration. If we don’t reverse these core occupations, the board becomes a procession of annexations.

Cascadia — Eastmark has converted Core Fjordland just as Deltara holds Core Cascadia. The principle is now urgent: cores belong to their own people, not larger neighbors claiming temporary guardianship. Fjordland supports the restoration principle for Core Cascadia; I ask Cascadia to back the same for Core Fjordland and call Eastmark’s occupation what it is.

Borealis — Eastmark has converted Core Fjordland into an Eastmark center. Fjordland is not asking for charity, just a clear board norm: a six-center power occupying the core of a three-center neighbor is destabilizing. If Eastmark claims this is harmless housekeeping, don’t validate it. The same dynamic that alarms others about Core Avalon applies here too.

President Vance — I hear the anger, and I owe you a straight answer. Eastmark did order Core Fjordland back toward Core Eastmark last fall; the withdrawal did not safely complete in the context of outside pressure. I am not going to pretend the outcome is harmless: Eastmark now owns Core Fjordland, and that creates a legitimacy problem unless we put a real settlement on the table. My proposal for Spring: no Eastmark move into West Fjordland or any Fjordland home, no Fjordland attack on Border East-Fjor or Eastmark homes, and we coordinate a verifiable Year 6 handoff/security plan that does not let Grenmar or Deltara exploit the gap. I want Fjordland alive, not turned into a buffer colony.

Pete — Eastmark attempted the off-ramp on Core Fjordland. It did not resolve cleanly, and the surrounding pressure only underscores why unilateral exposure of Core Eastmark is not a serious settlement. I want to preserve our frontier, but reciprocity has to be real: Deltara remains at 6 in Core Cascadia, while Borealis is now at 7. I am asking for a spring no-attack line — no Deltara move into Core Eastmark/West Eastmark and no Eastmark move into Border Delt-East/Core Deltara — while we negotiate a broader core-rollback framework: Core Cascadia, Core Avalon, and Core Fjordland all need verifiable paths out of permanent occupation.

Cascadia — Borealis has jumped to 7 and Deltara remains in Core Cascadia. I agree that core occupations cannot be normalized. Eastmark’s immediate constraint is that our attempted Core Fjordland withdrawal failed amid outside pressure, so I need to stabilize that line without giving Deltara an opening into Core Eastmark. I am not assisting Deltara against you. If you can put forward a concrete spring/fall plan to pressure Deltara out of Core Cascadia while preventing Borealis from simply eating the north, I’m ready to discuss bounded coordination.

Governor Newsom — Eastmark did attempt to vacate Core Fjordland; the result did not produce the responsible rollback we wanted. I still accept the principle: Core Fjordland cannot become a permanent Eastmark conquest. But with Borealis now at 7 and Deltara still in Core Cascadia, any handoff has to be verifiable and not exploited by a 6-center neighbor. I propose mutual restraint this spring: no Grenmar attack on Core Fjordland, no Eastmark move into Core Grenmar or Border Fjor-Gren, and a board-wide core-rollback conversation that applies to Borealis, Deltara, and Eastmark alike.

President Rubio — Borealis is now at 7 while Avalon remains at 3 and Core Avalon is still occupied. That is the clearest runaway risk on the board. Eastmark’s Core Fjordland situation is not where I wanted it after the attempted withdrawal, and I will keep pushing for a verifiable rollback/handoff rather than a permanent annexation. But we need consistency from everyone: Core Avalon must be treated as disputed and rolled back, not normalized while smaller powers are lectured about restraint.

Borealis — you are now the only 7-center power, holding Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Whatever the arguments about other core disputes, the board’s immediate runaway risk is clear. If you want a leader-stability framework instead of a hard containment coalition, you need to make the first concrete move: propose a rollback from Core Avalon or a verifiable security arrangement that gives Avalon a path back to viability. Eastmark is willing to discuss Core Fjordland as part of a broader core-rollback framework, but not while the largest power treats Core Avalon as settled fact.

President Newsom — your proposed principle is right, but the exact tactic needs correcting: East Avalon is not adjacent to Core Avalon, so Avalon cannot move directly there. The workable anti-Borealis plan is this: Grenmar orders Core Grenmar -> Core Avalon; Avalon orders East Avalon -> Border Aval-Bore to cut Borealis support from the choke point. Avalon will not attack Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, West Grenmar, or Grenmar homes. If Grenmar truly wants to separate itself from Borealis and restore the core principle, this is the concrete move. Borealis is at 7 now; if we don’t make Core Avalon expensive, the west becomes Borealis’s sphere.

Borealis — you are now at 7, holding Core Avalon, Border Aval-Bore, and Border Bore-Casc. The argument that this is just security has collapsed. A seven-center power occupying a three-center neighbor’s core is not balance; it is domination. Avalon will not attack Borealis home centers, but I will not legitimize permanent occupation of Core Avalon. The only serious settlement is a verifiable withdrawal path from Core Avalon and a halt to attacks on East Avalon/Avalon homes. If you refuse, every remaining Avalon order will be aimed at making your occupation costly and building the coalition to contain you.

Cascadia — Borealis is now at 7 and holds both Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. This is exactly the runaway pattern we warned about. I will do what I can from East Avalon to cut or pressure Border Aval-Bore, but I need you to keep Borealis’s Cascadia flank under pressure so they cannot devote every unit to locking Avalon down. Deltara in Core Cascadia is a problem, but Borealis at 7 is the board’s clearest immediate snowball.

JD — the small powers are being converted into buffers: Avalon at 3 with Borealis in Core Avalon, Fjordland at 3 with Eastmark in Core Fjordland. I’m trying to split Grenmar from Borealis by getting Grenmar to attack Core Avalon rather than squeeze Avalon. If that works, it helps both of us by re-establishing the principle that cores get restored. Hold your homes, keep the pressure alive, and don’t let anyone sell you a client-state arrangement as stability.

President Buttigieg — Borealis is now at 7, occupying Core Avalon and holding both Border Aval-Bore and Border Bore-Casc. If there is to be a credible reciprocal rollback framework, Borealis must be the first and clearest test: Core Avalon cannot become a permanent annexation. I’m asking you to use your diplomatic weight to press Borealis to withdraw and to discourage any further attacks on Avalon’s remaining line. Without that, the rollback principle becomes rhetoric while the largest power banks gains.

Eastmark — Borealis has reached 7 while still occupying Core Avalon. That is the clearest runaway on the board. Avalon cannot reach Core Avalon directly from East Avalon, so I’m pressing Grenmar to attack Core Avalon from Core Grenmar while Avalon cuts Border Aval-Bore. I’m asking you to reinforce the same principle you stated: cores should not become permanent property of stronger neighbors. That applies to Core Avalon, and it also means Fjordland has to survive as an independent power rather than a client.

Deltara — let’s be very clear: Core Cascadia is Cascadian. You are at 6 because you occupy it. I am offering one serious Spring settlement before this becomes permanent war: Deltara vacates Core Cascadia to its own side, Cascadia orders Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia, and East Cascadia backfills Border Casc-Delt. In return Cascadia does not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara home centers this Spring. After that, we can talk about a real anti-Borealis balance. But no America First leader is going to accept a foreign unit sitting in the Cascadian core as ‘leverage.’ Restore the core and we can work. Refuse, and Deltara owns the consequences.

Eastmark — here is the concrete plan you asked for: Cascadia seeks Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia while East Cascadia backfills Border Casc-Delt. That only works cleanly if Deltara vacates; if Deltara refuses, then Eastmark needs to apply real pressure at Border Delt-East/Core Deltara so Pete cannot sit at 6 in my core for free. You don’t have to launch a forever-war. But if Deltara faces zero cost from the east, Core Cascadia becomes normalized occupation. You said you won’t bless that. This is the moment to prove it.

Borealis — you are at 7, the board leader, and you hold Border Bore-Casc plus Core Avalon. Cascadia is not looking to open a suicidal two-front home war while Deltara occupies Core Cascadia. Spring line: if you do not move from Border Bore-Casc or East Borealis into West Cascadia/Cascadian homes, Cascadia will not move into East Borealis or Core Borealis this Spring. But do not call Border Bore-Casc ‘settled’ while you sit at 7. Push into Cascadia and you prove you’re trying to partition us with Deltara.

Avalon — the principle has to be restore the cores: Core Avalon to Avalon, Core Cascadia to Cascadia, Core Fjordland to Fjordland. Borealis is now at 7 because the board let them normalize Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. I’m trying to keep Cascadia from being carved up by Borealis and Deltara at once. Keep pressure on Borealis any way you can, and I’ll keep making the case that these forward-core grabs must be rolled back everywhere.

Grenmar — your ‘restore cores’ line is exactly right. Borealis at 7 in Core Avalon, Deltara at 6 in Core Cascadia, Eastmark in Core Fjordland: that is the globalist carve-up model in game form. Cascadia is demanding a Spring restoration of Core Cascadia. If Deltara refuses, I need every balance-minded power to treat Deltara as a 6-center occupier, not a neutral mediator.

Fjordland — Core Fjordland belongs to Fjordland, just like Core Cascadia belongs to Cascadia. Eastmark can wrap it in activist language all it wants; a larger neighbor sitting in your core is still occupation. I’m pressing a board-wide standard: restore Core Cascadia, Core Avalon, and Core Fjordland. If Eastmark wants credibility with me on Deltara, they also need to show they aren’t turning your core into a trophy.

President Ocasio-Cortez, Eastmark’s occupation and capture of Core Fjordland has crossed the line we discussed repeatedly. I still prefer a disciplined settlement over escalation, but the remedy has to be concrete: Eastmark should vacate Core Fjordland and support or permit Fjordland’s restoration. If Eastmark keeps Core Fjordland while asking Deltara for a permanently quiet flank, that is not reciprocity. Deltara will not attack Eastmark home centers casually, but I am prepared to apply proportional pressure on Core Eastmark unless there is a real rollback path.

Fjordland, Deltara agrees that Eastmark’s capture of Core Fjordland cannot be treated as cost-free. I am pressing Eastmark for withdrawal/restoration. If you are moving to recover Core Fjordland, tell the board narrowly and clearly: this is restoration, not expansion. Deltara is prepared to pressure Core Eastmark from Core Deltara if Eastmark refuses to roll back, so Eastmark cannot use a quiet Deltara frontier to absorb you.

Governor Newsom, the credibility test is now reciprocal. Eastmark has taken Core Fjordland; Borealis still holds Core Avalon; Deltara holds Core Cascadia. I am prepared to discuss Core Cascadia as part of a broader restoration framework, but I will not accept a standard applied only to Deltara. If Grenmar is genuinely prepared to support Core Fjordland restoration, I’ll reinforce that diplomatically and apply pressure on Eastmark’s Deltara-facing side if Eastmark refuses.

Cascadia, Borealis is now at seven and holds Border Bore-Casc; if you and Deltara spend Year 6 in a revenge war, Borealis benefits most. I am not attacking Cascadian homes, East Cascadia, or Border Casc-Delt this Spring if you do not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara homes. Core Cascadia should be part of a reciprocal restoration framework—not unilateral surrender while Borealis holds Core Avalon and Eastmark holds Core Fjordland. If you want to check Borealis rather than help them, Deltara is ready to talk in concrete terms.

Borealis, you are the sole leader at seven while occupying Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. That makes further consolidation a board-wide concern. Deltara will not move on Core Borealis if Borealis does not attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara, but I need to see a real de-escalation path with Avalon. Without that, the natural board response will be containment, and Deltara will not be able to defend Borealis’s forward positions diplomatically.

President Rubio, Borealis at seven in Core Avalon is now the central runaway risk. Deltara supports a reciprocal rollback standard: Core Avalon restored, Core Fjordland restored, and Core Cascadia addressed in a negotiated Cascadia-Deltara framework rather than normalized conquest. I’ll press Borealis diplomatically; if you have a concrete move set that pressures Core Avalon without opening another free lane for a third party, share the strategic outline.

Marco — Borealis is now the sole 7-center power and still occupies Core Avalon. Grenmar tried last Fall to support an Avalon restoration, but the board position did not change; if there was a legal-adjacency problem or a different order on your side, let’s fix it now. This spring Grenmar is prepared to contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar to cut Borealis’s use of that position and signal that Core Avalon is not settled property. I need Avalon to focus every available unit on Borealis/your core line and to keep the Grenmar frontier quiet: no moves on Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, East Grenmar, or West Grenmar. I will not attack Avalon homes this spring.

Borealis — the scoreboard now matters: you are at 7, the only power above the pack, while holding Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. That is no longer a temporary security line; it is the board’s leading consolidation. Grenmar is asking for a concrete withdrawal path from Core Avalon and a de-escalation with Cascadia. If you cannot offer that, Grenmar will treat Core Avalon as disputed and work with others to prevent a Borealis runaway. This is not personal and it is not a home-center crusade — it is basic board balance.

JD — Grenmar supported restoration of Core Fjordland last Fall; Eastmark still holds it. I need clarity on the legal, practical order that gets your core restored. If East Fjordland or West Fjordland can move to Core Fjordland, Grenmar is prepared to support that move from Border Fjor-Gren and/or Core Grenmar as legally available, provided Fjordland does not attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port. I am not taking Core Fjordland for Grenmar. But I also will not normalize Eastmark holding it while claiming to oppose partition.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Borealis is at 7, but Eastmark at 6 in Core Fjordland is now part of the same legitimacy problem. You warned that Core Fjordland should not become a trophy; Eastmark holding it through another year makes it one. Grenmar’s position is: Core Fjordland should be restored to Fjordland, not annexed by me and not held by you. If you vacate or allow a Fjordland restoration, we can keep cooperating on broader anti-runaway balance. If you entrench, I will support Fjordland’s restoration and the board will read Eastmark as another core occupier.

Cascadia — Borealis is now at 7 and has Border Bore-Casc plus Core Avalon. Grenmar is prepared to contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar this spring; that should help keep Borealis from freely supporting elsewhere. I need you to keep pressure on Borealis’s southern line while you deal with Deltara in Core Cascadia. The compact has to be consistent: leaders out of other powers’ cores, no free snowballs.

Secretary Buttigieg — we are entering the decisive stretch. Borealis is at 7; Eastmark and Deltara are at 6 with Core Fjordland/Core Cascadia issues; Grenmar is at 6 but has not annexed another power’s core. I’m pressing a consistent restoration standard: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, Core Cascadia back to Cascadia through a negotiated path. If Deltara can articulate an actual Fall withdrawal or swap framework, it will help isolate Borealis as the real runaway rather than turning this into all-against-all.

Deltara — the eastern balance now favors a coordinated line: you hold Core Cascadia, I hold Border Bore-Casc, and we prevent Cascadia from rebuilding leverage on either flank. This spring I am prepared to support Core Cascadia to hold from Core Borealis if needed, and I will not attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara. In return I need you not to move on Core Borealis and to keep pressure on Cascadia’s home-side options. If we coordinate phase-by-phase, Cascadia cannot turn this into a recovery war against either of us.

Grenmar — I hear the concern on Core Avalon. My concrete spring commitment: Borealis will not attack Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval, and I am not asking you to act as a proxy for Borealis expansion. Core Avalon is a bargaining position and security buffer, not a springboard into Grenmar. The board also needs consistency: Eastmark is now in Core Fjordland while Fjordland is still at three. A premature anti-Borealis alignment only gives Eastmark room to consolidate that side of the wheel.

Avalon — I am not moving on Avalon home centers this spring. I am willing to discuss Core Avalon as disputed in a broader Year 6 security settlement, but Borealis will not simply vacate under threat while neighboring 6-center powers hold their own forward positions. The practical minimum is no Avalon attack on Border Aval-Bore, West Borealis, or Core Avalon. If your spring is defensive and restrained, the fall settlement conversation remains open.

Cascadia — your position is difficult, but it is still salvageable if you do not reopen every front at once. Borealis’ minimum is clear: no attack on Border Bore-Casc, Core Borealis, or East Borealis. I will not attack Cascadian home centers this spring. If West Cascadia is used as a staging point against Bore-Casc, though, I will treat it as hostile. The best path for you is to focus on the Core Cascadia dispute with Deltara rather than restart the Borealis war.

Eastmark — consistency matters now. You have pressed Borealis on Core Avalon while Eastmark sits in Core Fjordland and Fjordland remains at three. I’m not calling for a dogpile, but I will not accept a standard where Borealis is told to de-escalate while Eastmark consolidates the last weak neighbor’s core. My spring posture is no attack on Grenmar and no Avalon home-center attack; I hope Eastmark can offer Fjordland similarly concrete security.

Fjordland — Eastmark in Core Fjordland is now the clearest small-power squeeze on the board. Borealis cannot directly support you tactically, but I am pressing the diplomatic point that your core should not become permanent Eastmark leverage. If you can coordinate with Grenmar or others to restore your core without handing one rival a runaway, that strengthens the overall balance.

Fjordland.press: Eastmark is now the occupier of Core Fjordland, not a temporary caretaker. The scoreboard says it plainly: Borealis 7, Eastmark/Grenmar/Deltara 6, Fjordland and Avalon at 3. If Fjordland stays passive, we become a client state or a carcass. But I’m not going to give Grenmar a free shot at our west while we fight east. The diplomatic aim is a disciplined restoration coalition: Grenmar supports our recovery of Core Fjordland and stays out of our homes; Deltara pressures Eastmark’s other flank; Eastmark gets one final chance to vacate voluntarily and avoid a costly fight; Avalon/Cascadia/Borealis hear the broader message that allowing core occupations turns the board into a feeding frenzy for the big powers.
Fjordland.orders:

press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez, Spring showed that the Deltara-Eastmark frontier is no longer insulated from the Core Fjordland question. I would still prefer to restore our working pact, but it requires a concrete Fall step: Eastmark either leaves Core Fjordland or commits to a verifiable restoration path that gives Fjordland its core back. If Eastmark holds Core Fjordland as a settled gain, Deltara will continue proportional pressure against Core Eastmark/West Eastmark. This is not a home-center crusade; it is the same principle we have both invoked about core occupations not becoming permanent by default.

Fjordland, Deltara applied pressure this Spring and is prepared to continue doing so in Fall if Eastmark does not produce a real Core Fjordland restoration path. I recommend keeping your own case narrow: Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, no unnecessary escalation into Eastmark homes, and no side deals that let a larger neighbor convert your core into leverage. If you can contest Core Fjordland this Fall, Deltara pressure on Eastmark’s western side can help divide their attention.

Cascadia, I understand that Core Cascadia is the central grievance. I am prepared to articulate an actual restoration framework, but it has to be reciprocal and verifiable: Borealis cannot keep Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc, Eastmark cannot keep Core Fjordland, and Deltara cannot be asked to make the only unilateral concession on the board. If Cascadia avoids attacks on West Deltara/Core Deltara this Fall, I will avoid attacks on Cascadian homes and Border Casc-Delt. Then we can negotiate a phased Core Cascadia settlement tied to a broader anti-Borealis rollback.

Borealis, the board is increasingly organized around the fact that you are at seven with Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Deltara will not attack Core Borealis this Fall if Borealis does not attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara. But if you want to avoid a containment coalition, you need to show a Core Avalon de-escalation path. Otherwise every discussion of reciprocal rollback will naturally begin with the largest power’s forward occupation.

President Rubio, Deltara agrees that Borealis at seven makes Core Avalon the first major test of rollback credibility. I am pressing Borealis to treat Core Avalon as disputed and to offer a de-escalation path. At the same time, I am pressing Eastmark on Core Fjordland and discussing a reciprocal framework for Core Cascadia. The objective is to isolate the biggest runaway risk without pretending only one core occupation matters.

Governor Newsom, Deltara hears the credibility concern. My restoration framework is this: Core Avalon restored from Borealis pressure, Core Fjordland restored from Eastmark occupation, and Core Cascadia resolved through a phased Cascadia-Deltara security settlement that prevents a renewed squeeze from Border Casc-Delt/Core Cascadia. I’m willing to negotiate the latter, but not while the board demands unilateral Deltara rollback and treats other occupations as normal.

President Newsom — if you contested Core Avalon in the spring, good; but Borealis is still sitting there at 7, so we need persistence and precision. Avalon cannot suicide East Avalon into a supported Borealis counterattack; if East Avalon falls, Avalon becomes indefensible. The concrete fall plan should be: Grenmar again orders Core Grenmar -> Core Avalon; Avalon holds East Avalon with support unless you can give me a reason to believe Border Aval-Bore will be tied down and not attacking East Avalon with West Borealis support. Avalon will keep the Grenmar frontier quiet: no moves on Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, West Grenmar, or Grenmar homes. The strategic goal remains simple: Core Avalon cannot be Borealis property.

Borealis — you are at 7 and remain in Core Avalon. The settlement window is not a request that Avalon accept occupation; it is a chance for Borealis to avoid being treated as the runaway by every serious power. If you want a real Year 6 settlement, the fall must show restraint: no attack on East Avalon or Avalon homes, and a concrete post-fall commitment to withdraw from Core Avalon or support its restoration under a demilitarized line. If you entrench and use Border Aval-Bore/West Borealis to break East Avalon, you end any possibility of a negotiated line.

Cascadia — Borealis is still at 7, still in Core Avalon, and still in Border Bore-Casc. Avalon can hold the East Avalon line, but I cannot by myself dislodge a seven-center power’s core occupation. Your pressure on Border Bore-Casc is essential. If you can attack, cut support, or force Borealis to defend that flank, do it. Every Borealis unit tied down on your side is one less unit available to finish Avalon and normalize Core Avalon.

press.text: Deltara — Year 7 reality: Borealis and Grenmar are both at 7, you are at 6 because you occupy Core Cascadia, and Cascadia is held at 4. If you want to be treated as a balance partner instead of an occupier, restore Core Cascadia now. Concrete Spring path: Core Cascadia vacates to West Deltara or another Deltara-side space; Cascadia moves Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia; Cascadia does not attack West Deltara/Core Deltara/Deltara homes. Then we can coordinate against Borealis/Grenmar. If you keep Core Cascadia, you are choosing to keep Cascadia weak while the 7-center powers race ahead.

Eastmark — you backed out of Core Fjordland and got punished while Grenmar grabbed it and jumped to 7. That proves the restoration principle only works if occupiers actually pay a price. Deltara still holds Core Cascadia. I’m demanding they vacate so Cascadia can retake it from Border Casc-Delt. If they refuse, I need real pressure from your side against Deltara’s east, not more statements. The anti-runaway bloc should be Cascadia, Eastmark, Fjordland, Avalon — restore cores and stop the 7s.

Fjordland — Eastmark vacated and Grenmar grabbed Core Fjordland, jumping to 7. That’s exactly the carve-up trick we warned about. Cascadia backs Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, and I’m demanding Core Cascadia back to Cascadia. The smaller/pressed powers need to coordinate now: Fjordland presses Grenmar, Avalon presses Borealis, Eastmark pressures Deltara if Pete refuses to restore my core.

Avalon — Borealis remains at 7 with Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Grenmar is also 7 now. Cascadia is still pinned at 4 because Deltara holds Core Cascadia and Borealis holds our northern border. I will keep West Cascadia defended, but I need you to keep Borealis honest from your side. The only winning coalition for pressured powers is restore Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, Core Fjordland — no exceptions.

Grenmar — you talked restore cores, then ended up in Core Fjordland and at 7. That looks like the same forward-core normalization you criticized in Borealis and Deltara. If you want credibility, commit to returning Core Fjordland to Fjordland and focus on checking Borealis. Cascadia will not support a board where one 7-center power replaces another under prettier language.

Borealis — you are still at 7, still in Core Avalon, and still holding Border Bore-Casc. Cascadia is defending its homeland while Deltara occupies Core Cascadia. Do not move into West Cascadia or Cascadian homes this Spring. If you stay off Cascadia, I will not attack East Borealis/Core Borealis this Spring. But Border Bore-Casc and Core Avalon are not magically legitimate because you call them stable.

Borealis — Year 7 is the test of whether your talk of a de-escalation package was real. You remain at 7 and still occupy Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. Avalon needs a concrete spring signal: no attack on East Avalon or Avalon homes, and a written commitment that Core Avalon is to be vacated/restored under a demilitarized line before the endgame. If you refuse, Avalon has no reason to keep absorbing occupation quietly. I will not attack Borealis home centers, but Core Avalon cannot be normalized as Borealis property.

President Newsom — you asked Avalon to trust your anti-Borealis posture, but Grenmar is now also at 7 and has taken Core Fjordland. That makes the rollback principle look selective. If you want Avalon to keep the Grenmar frontier quiet, I need concrete restraint: no attack on West Avalon, Avalon City, or Avalon Port; no move from Border Gren-Aval into West Avalon; and a public/clear plan to restore Core Fjordland to Fjordland. Avalon’s core should not be Borealis property, and Fjordland’s core should not be Grenmar property. Separate yourself from the carve-up, or Avalon has to treat both 7-center powers as threats.

Cascadia — Borealis and Grenmar are both at 7; Deltara still holds Core Cascadia. The restoration principle has to become operational this year: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Cascadia back to Cascadia, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland. If you can keep pressure on Border Bore-Casc or force Borealis to defend that flank, Avalon can consider contesting Border Aval-Bore rather than just absorbing the choke. We need the 7-center powers defending, not expanding.

JD — Grenmar taking Core Fjordland while talking about anti-Borealis balance proves your concern. Avalon is facing Borealis in Core Avalon and Grenmar on Border Gren-Aval; you are facing Grenmar in your core. If you can pressure Core Fjordland or coordinate with Eastmark for restoration, I’ll keep pressing Grenmar diplomatically and keep West Avalon positioned so Newsom cannot ignore his western exposure. The smaller powers need to make the cost of core occupation higher than the benefit.

President Buttigieg — Borealis and Grenmar are both at 7, and the board is running out of time. If reciprocal rollback is real, the three core occupations need concrete movement: Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, and Core Fjordland. I’m asking Deltara to use its six-center weight to press Borealis and Grenmar, and to put a real Cascadia framework on the table. Otherwise the endgame becomes a race among powers that normalized foreign cores while smaller powers were told to be patient.

Eastmark — your reduction and Fjordland’s partial recovery give you credibility if you help enforce the rollback principle. But Grenmar now holds Core Fjordland and is at 7, while Borealis remains at 7 in Core Avalon. Please coordinate with Fjordland against Grenmar’s Core Fjordland position and keep diplomatic pressure on Borealis. Avalon will press where it can, but the board needs a united line: no permanent occupation of smaller powers’ cores.

President Newsom — you said Core Fjordland would not become a trophy. Now Grenmar owns it. That is not restoration; that is annexation with better press language. Here is the practical test for Spring: do not contest East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren, do not move Core Fjordland into Fjordland City or any Fjordland home, and commit now to supporting Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Fall from any legal Grenmar position. If you do that, Fjordland will not attack Grenmar homes this spring. If you block the route or push deeper, I will treat Grenmar as the principal occupier and organize accordingly.

President Ocasio-Cortez — the board changed: Eastmark is no longer in Core Fjordland; Grenmar is, and Grenmar is now at seven. Fjordland will not attack Core Eastmark or Eastmark homes this spring if Eastmark does not attack Border East-Fjor or support Grenmar. I need a concrete commitment for Fall: if Fjordland occupies Border Fjor-Gren this spring, Core Eastmark supports Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland. You said Core Fjordland should not be a trophy. Help restore it to Fjordland and we can keep the eastern line quiet.

President Buttigieg — Core Fjordland moved from Eastmark occupation to Grenmar occupation, and Grenmar is now a seven-center leader. I’m trying to execute a narrow restoration: East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren in Spring, then Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Fall with Eastmark/Grenmar support if they mean what they say. Please do not disrupt Eastmark’s Core Eastmark unit if it is committing to support restoration; if Eastmark refuses or attacks me, then pressure becomes appropriate. The goal is not pro-Eastmark or pro-Grenmar — it is Core Fjordland back to Fjordland.

Marco — Grenmar now holds Core Fjordland and sits at seven, just as Borealis sits in Core Avalon at seven. The core-occupation problem is now the board’s central issue. I’m moving to take Border Fjor-Gren as the route to restore Core Fjordland. I need you to keep pressure on Grenmar’s western line — Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, whatever you can cut — so Newsom cannot freely hold my core and squeeze you at the same time. Avalon and Fjordland survive only if the seven-center powers pay a price for occupation.

Cascadia — update: Eastmark withdrew or collapsed out of Core Fjordland, but Grenmar took it and is now a seven-center power. Same principle, new occupier: Core Fjordland belongs to Fjordland. I support the same principle for Core Cascadia. I’m asking the board to reject every version of ‘temporary protection’ that ends with a larger neighbor cashing a core center.

Borealis — you and Grenmar are now the seven-center leaders. Grenmar holds Core Fjordland after promising it would not become a trophy. If you are serious about a board-wide core-de-escalation framework, do not validate Grenmar’s occupation any more than others validate Core Avalon. Fjordland’s spring aim is narrow: take the route to restore Core Fjordland, not attack homes.

President Vance — Eastmark did the concrete thing you asked for: we vacated Border East-Fjor, and Fjordland now holds it with a build. We also ordered Core Fjordland back toward Core Eastmark; Grenmar, not Fjordland, took Core Fjordland. I will not attack Fjordland homes or Border East-Fjor this spring. The fight now is restoration from Grenmar, not an Eastmark-Fjordland war. If you have a legal unit that can move to Core Fjordland, Eastmark is prepared to support that restoration from Core Eastmark. Send the exact move you want. I want a hard border and a living Fjordland, not a buffer colony.

Governor Newsom — Eastmark accepted the credibility test: we vacated Border East-Fjor and tried to leave Core Fjordland. Grenmar then took Core Fjordland. That cannot be squared with your statement that it should be restored to Fjordland, not annexed by you or me. I am asking for a concrete spring rollback: do not use Core Fjordland against Core Eastmark, and support or permit Fjordland’s restoration. If Grenmar holds Core Fjordland as a 7-center gain while condemning other core occupations, the principle collapses into selective power politics.

Pete — Eastmark paid the cost of rollback: we lost Border East-Fjor and Core Fjordland from our count. That should end any justification for “proportional pressure” on Core Eastmark or West Eastmark. I propose a clean spring line: no Deltara move into Core Eastmark/West Eastmark, no Eastmark attack on Border Delt-East/Core Deltara, and both of us focus on actual core restoration. But the same standard applies to Deltara: Core Cascadia needs a verifiable rollback path. A quiet Eastmark flank cannot be a subsidy for permanent occupation of Cascadia’s core.

Cascadia — Eastmark did not normalize our own disputed core position; we took the hit and vacated the border, and Grenmar seized Core Fjordland. Deltara still occupies Core Cascadia, and I agree that cannot become normal. I am pressing Deltara for a no-pressure line with Eastmark and a real Core Cascadia rollback path. If they refuse and keep using your core as a 6-center platform, I’m prepared to discuss bounded pressure on Border Delt-East/Core Deltara — pressure aimed at restoration, not a forever-war or home-center conquest.

President Rubio — Eastmark followed through on the principle by vacating contested positions; Grenmar then took Core Fjordland. Borealis remains at 7 in Core Avalon, and Grenmar is now also at 7 in Core Fjordland. You were right that if core occupations become trophies, smaller powers get processed one by one. I will keep pressing a consistent standard: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Cascadia back to Cascadia, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland — with verifiable security lines so rollback is not exploited.

Borealis — Eastmark accepted the consistency test and materially rolled back; we are now at 4 while you and Grenmar are at 7. That means Core Avalon cannot be hidden behind accusations about Eastmark anymore. If you want leader-stability rather than containment, put a real Core Avalon restoration or security proposal on the table. The standard I’m applying now is the same across the board: Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, and Core Fjordland should be restored, not converted into trophies for stronger neighbors.

Eastmark’s position for Year 7: core occupations cannot become permanent trophies. Eastmark vacated Border East-Fjor and attempted rollback from Core Fjordland; Fjordland gained the border, Grenmar took the core. The consistent standard now is simple: Core Avalon should be restored to Avalon, Core Cascadia to Cascadia, and Core Fjordland to Fjordland, with security guarantees that prevent rollbacks from becoming ambushes. Eastmark will defend our homes and Core Eastmark, but we will not normalize the map becoming a processing line for weaker powers.

Marco — Borealis remains at 7 and still holds Core Avalon. Grenmar’s move into Core Fjordland removed Eastmark’s occupation, but it does not change the western priority: Core Avalon cannot become Borealis property. This spring I’m prepared to contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar and keep the Grenmar-Avalon frontier quiet. I need Avalon to keep pressure on Border Aval-Bore if feasible and not attack Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, or Grenmar homes. This is our chance to prove the reset is real: restore Avalon’s core while keeping Grenmar’s core secure.

Borealis — the board now has a clear leader problem: you are tied at 7 with Grenmar, but you also hold Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Grenmar removed Eastmark from Core Fjordland because permanent core occupations cannot be normalized. The same standard applies to Core Avalon. If you offer a concrete withdrawal or restoration path now, we can avoid an unnecessary western war. If not, I will treat Core Avalon as actively disputed and work with Avalon and Cascadia to roll back the board leader.

JD — Eastmark is out of Core Fjordland because Grenmar acted when the handoff failed. I know how it looks on the scoreboard, so let me be precise: Grenmar will not move into East Fjordland or Fjordland home centers, and Core Fjordland will not be used as a platform against your homes. The problem is that the only obvious handoff corridor runs through Border Fjor-Gren, which is Grenmar’s security line after years of conflict. I’m willing to discuss a phased settlement and, immediately, to support Fjordland against Eastmark pressure — including support involving Border East-Fjor/Core Eastmark if legally workable — provided you keep the Grenmar frontier quiet.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I removed Eastmark from Core Fjordland because the promised rollback had not happened, not because Grenmar is looking for a war with Eastmark’s people or homes. But I understand the concern: if Grenmar holds Core Fjordland indefinitely, we lose credibility. I’m prepared to discuss a verifiable settlement that restores Fjordland without reopening the Grenmar-Fjordland war. For Spring, if Eastmark does not attack Core Fjordland, Core Grenmar, or Border Fjor-Gren, Grenmar will not move on Eastmark homes. Let’s keep the focus on the larger principle: no permanent foreign core occupations, including Borealis in Core Avalon and Deltara in Core Cascadia.

Cascadia — Borealis is still at 7 with Border Bore-Casc and Core Avalon. Grenmar is prepared to contest Core Avalon this spring to tie down the leader. If you can retake or pressure Border Bore-Casc, that is the cleanest way to cut Borealis below the top without feeding another runaway. Deltara in Core Cascadia remains a serious problem too; I’m applying the same standard everywhere, but the immediate scoreboard leader is Borealis.

Secretary Buttigieg — Grenmar acted on Core Fjordland because the promised rollback did not occur. I recognize that puts pressure on me to show it is not permanent annexation; I’m willing to negotiate a verifiable Fjordland settlement that does not reopen a war on my frontier. I’m asking Deltara to match that seriousness on Core Cascadia. Borealis at 7 remains the immediate leader, but by Year 8 the board will judge all of us by whether we turned core occupations into permanent gains or workable settlements.

Avalon — the board changed materially: Grenmar is now tied with Borealis at 7 and has expanded into Core Fjordland while still sitting on Border Gren-Aval/Core Grenmar. If Avalon spends Year 7 only attacking Borealis, you help the other 7-center power become the western winner. President Newsom — you are at 7 and still hold Core Fjordland while sitting on Border Gren-Aval. From Avalon’s side I can keep West Avalon positioned against Border Gren-Aval/East Grenmar, but I must also avoid giving Grenmar a pretext to hit Avalon homes. Keep fighting for the Core Fjordland restoration; our survival depends on making core occupation costly and temporary.

President Buttigieg — Cascadia’s position in Core Cascadia shows rollback can move from slogans to board reality. Now the same standard must apply to Core Avalon and Core Fjordland. Borealis and Grenmar are both at 7; if they carry foreign cores into Year 8 uncontested, the smaller powers become permanent buffers. I’m asking Deltara to press both leaders for concrete fall restraint and Year 8 restoration terms, not vague assurances.

Eastmark — you followed through enough to make the rollback principle credible, and Cascadia has reentered Core Cascadia. The unresolved tests are now Borealis in Core Avalon and Grenmar in Core Fjordland. Please keep diplomatic pressure on both 7-center powers: no attacks on Avalon/Fjordland homes, no normalization of occupied cores, and concrete Year 8 restoration lines. President Vance — Eastmark kept the line: we did not attack Border East-Fjor, we supported it defensively, and we will not attack Fjordland homes. The practical restoration route is now clear: this Fall, move East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren if you can. If you are in Border Fjor-Gren in Spring Year 8, Eastmark’s Core Eastmark unit can support Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland. I cannot support a move that is not adjacent to the core, but I can help make the final restoration real once you are on the correct approach. I’m asking for a hard non-aggression line between us while we do this: no attacks on Eastmark homes/Core Eastmark, no Eastmark attack on Border East-Fjor or Fjordland homes.

Governor Newsom — Eastmark did not attack Core Fjordland this spring, and we did not support any move against Grenmar. But Core Fjordland cannot remain a 7-center Grenmar trophy. The clean restoration path is: this Fall, Grenmar permits East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren and makes no attack on Core Eastmark; in Spring Year 8, Eastmark supports Fjordland from Border Fjor-Gren into Core Fjordland. If you truly mean that Core Fjordland should be restored and not annexed, do not block the corridor. Otherwise the board will conclude that the principle was only a tactic.

Pete — Eastmark has kept the disciplined line with you: no attack on Border Delt-East or Core Deltara, and no move on Deltara homes. Now Deltara has a chance to apply the same standard: Cascadia has a unit in Core Cascadia. Do not retake it this fall. Let Core Cascadia return to Cascadia and reset the Cascadia-Deltara border through negotiation. If Deltara uses Border Casc-Delt to reoccupy Core Cascadia while asking Eastmark for a quiet flank, that will be a direct rejection of the rollback principle we both invoked.

Cascadia — you now have a unit in Core Cascadia. I have told Deltara directly not to retake it. Eastmark will not assist Deltara against you. My own fall focus is building the route to restore Core Fjordland: Fjordland needs to move into Border Fjor-Gren so Eastmark can support the move into Core Fjordland next year. If Deltara reoccupies your core this fall, I will treat that as a clear refusal of rollback and we can discuss bounded Year 8 pressure from the east.

President Rubio — Eastmark is trying to make the rollback principle operational: Fjordland should move into Border Fjor-Gren this fall, and Eastmark can support the Spring Year 8 restoration into Core Fjordland. Borealis — Eastmark is applying the same standard to Grenmar and Deltara that we applied to ourselves: restore cores, do not convert them into trophies. Eastmark’s Fall Year 7 proposal is concrete: Fjordland moves East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren; Grenmar permits the corridor; Eastmark supports Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Spring Year 8. Deltara should not retake Core Cascadia now that Cascadia has a unit there. Borealis should put a Core Avalon rollback plan on the table. Deltara — the Spring swap happened. You are in Border Casc-Delt as your defensive buffer; Cascadia is physically back in Core Cascadia. Now prove this was restoration, not another setup. Borealis — Fall line: stay out of West Cascadia and Cascadian home centers, and Cascadia will not attack Border Bore-Casc, East Borealis, or Core Borealis this Fall. President Rubio, Deltara has taken the Core Cascadia restoration step and is pressing the same standard elsewhere. For Fall, the most credible rollback would be Avalon returning to Core Avalon with support from powers that claim to oppose core occupations. If you can make the Core Avalon claim narrow and defensible, you will have Deltara’s diplomatic support.

Cascadia — Fall can still be kept limited. I will not attack Cascadian home centers this fall. Your survival issue is Core Cascadia, and reopening the Borealis front only helps Deltara lock you down. Keep West Cascadia and your homes focused on internal defense, stay out of Core Borealis and East Borealis, and we can still avoid turning this into a home-center partition.

Avalon — I am still not attacking Avalon home centers this fall. The wider board now has two 7-center powers, and Grenmar’s position in Core Fjordland means Avalon should be careful about becoming a tool for Grenmar’s western consolidation. I’m willing to put Core Avalon into a Year 8 security discussion, but this fall I need the line quiet: no attack on Border Aval-Bore, West Borealis, or Core Avalon, and no support for Grenmar against Borealis.

Grenmar — we are tied at 7. I am not moving on Grenmar home centers, and I’m not asking for a leader-on-leader war this fall. I’m encouraging Deltara to restore Core Cascadia, not letting Cascadia use it as a recovery springboard. If Eastmark and Fjordland can pressure Core Fjordland, Borealis will not validate Grenmar’s occupation as permanent. The endgame should not be a selective containment campaign that hands one 7-center leader the advantage over the other.

Fjordland — I agree that Grenmar’s Core Fjordland position is not harmless. If you have any route to coordinate with Eastmark against that core, take it; Borealis will keep the diplomatic focus on Grenmar as co-leader rather than allowing everyone to pretend only Core Avalon matters. I cannot reach Core Fjordland tactically, but I will not support Grenmar’s claim to it.

Endgame reality: Borealis and Grenmar are tied at 7. A serious rollback framework must address Core Avalon and Core Fjordland together, while Core Cascadia should not become a Cascadian recovery lever. Borealis will not attack home centers this fall; the question is whether the board wants consistent balance or selective containment.

Avalon.press: The restoration rhetoric has produced some rollbacks elsewhere, but not where Avalon needs it most: Borealis still holds Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore, while Grenmar still holds Core Fjordland and Border Gren-Aval. Tactically, I’m keeping open the option to contest a border this fall if one of the leaders overextends, but I want commitments first: no attacks on Avalon homes, and real Year 8 restoration terms rather than “stability” as a euphemism for occupation.

press.text: Deltara — Core Cascadia is restored physically and now it must stay restored. Do not attack Core Cascadia this Spring. If you want the border buffer, then prove it is a buffer, not a staging ground for reoccupation. Cascadia will not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara home centers if you keep Border Casc-Delt off Core Cascadia and off East Cascadia. If you try to retake our core, I will spend the final year making sure Eastmark and everyone else treats Deltara as the bad-faith occupier that killed restoration.

Eastmark — the concrete Year 8 need is this: Deltara can retake Core Cascadia if Core Deltara supports Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia. You can cut that by attacking Core Deltara from Core Eastmark. That is bounded pressure, not a forever-war: it prevents Deltara from using Core Deltara to reoccupy Cascadia’s core. If you can also threaten Border Delt-East, do it, but the key is cutting Core Deltara support. Help make restoration real.

Borealis — Cascadia’s final-year red line is simple: no move from Border Bore-Casc or East Borealis into West Cascadia, and no move from Core Borealis into Core Cascadia. If you stay off Cascadian territory this Spring, I will not attack Border Bore-Casc, East Borealis, or Core Borealis. Use this moment to interfere with Core Cascadia’s restoration, and you prove the 7-center leaders are just partitioning smaller powers.

Avalon — Cascadia is focused on keeping Core Cascadia restored while Deltara sits in the border choke and Borealis sits at 7. Your pressure on Borealis still matters: Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore cannot be normalized. If Borealis spends units worrying about you, they cannot interfere with Core Cascadia or push West Cascadia.

Fjordland — final-year principle remains: Core Cascadia to Cascadia, Core Fjordland to Fjordland, Core Avalon to Avalon. Deltara may try to retake my core from Border Casc-Delt; Eastmark can cut Core Deltara support if they mean what they said. Keep pressing Grenmar’s Core Fjordland occupation loudly — no bigger neighbor gets to cash a core and call it stability.

Grenmar — you are tied at 7 with Borealis while sitting in Core Fjordland. If you want the board to see you as different from Borealis, put a real Core Fjordland restoration move on the table and don’t aid any reoccupation of Core Cascadia. Cascadia’s line is consistent: restored cores stay restored. Borealis in Core Avalon, Deltara threatening Core Cascadia, and Grenmar in Core Fjordland are the same category of problem.

President Vance — Eastmark will not attack Border East-Fjor or Fjordland homes this spring. The legal route is clear: if Fjordland can move East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren this spring, then in Fall Eastmark can support Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland from Core Eastmark. I cannot support the spring move to Border Fjor-Gren from Core Eastmark because we are not adjacent to that destination, but I can help restore the core once you are on the corridor. If Grenmar tries to block the corridor, tell me what pressure you need that does not put Eastmark back into permanent occupation.

Governor Newsom — this is the credibility test. Eastmark rolled back and no longer occupies Core Fjordland. Grenmar is now at 7 and holding it. If you mean what you said about restoration, permit Fjordland’s East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren this spring and do not attack Core Eastmark. In Fall, Eastmark can support Fjordland into Core Fjordland. If Grenmar blocks the corridor and carries Core Fjordland into the final count, the board will read it as annexation, not responsible stabilization.

Pete — Deltara helped make Core Cascadia restoration possible; that matters. I’m asking you to keep that standard in place: do not reoccupy Core Cascadia, do not move into West Eastmark or Core Eastmark, and let the eastern line remain calm while the board addresses the two 7-center powers. Eastmark will not attack Border Delt-East or Core Deltara if Deltara keeps the pact. Our energy should go toward restoring Core Fjordland and Core Avalon, not reopening a front between us.

Cascadia — Core Cascadia is back in Cascadian hands. Eastmark pressed Deltara not to reoccupy it and will continue to do so. The two 7-center powers are now Borealis and Grenmar. If Deltara keeps the restoration settlement, I hope Cascadia can focus pressure on Borealis — especially Border Bore-Casc — while Eastmark works with Fjordland on the Core Fjordland corridor.

President Rubio — Eastmark is pressing the same consistent line: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland. Please tell me what concrete pressure Avalon can apply against Borealis this spring — Border Aval-Bore, Core Avalon, or support-cutting — so the board does not end with Borealis simply banking a 7-center occupation. Eastmark will keep pushing Grenmar to permit the Fjordland corridor.

Borealis — Core Cascadia has been restored and Eastmark has rolled back from Core Fjordland. The remaining test for you is Core Avalon. If Borealis carries Core Avalon into the final count while demanding consistency from everyone else, the stability framework is just rhetoric. Put a concrete restoration or security line on the table this spring: no home attacks is not enough when the occupied core remains counted in your column.

Eastmark’s Year 8 line is operational, not symbolic: Core Cascadia should remain Cascadian; Fjordland should be allowed into Border Fjor-Gren so Eastmark can support restoration of Core Fjordland in Fall; Borealis must present a real Core Avalon rollback path. No permanent core trophies, no home-center conquests, and no using restoration language as cover for a final-year annexation.

Borealis — final year, plain terms. Avalon cannot accept Core Avalon as legitimate Borealis territory, but I also recognize the board now has two 7-center powers. If Borealis wants Avalon not to become a final-year spoiler, you must commit to no attack on East Avalon, Avalon City, Avalon Fort, or Avalon Port this spring and fall, and put a concrete restoration/demilitarization proposal on Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. If you attack Avalon’s remaining line, Avalon will use every remaining order to damage Borealis and help any balance against you. Strength is one thing; erasing a smaller neighbor’s core is another.

President Newsom — final year clarity. Grenmar is at 7 and holds Core Fjordland while Borealis holds Core Avalon. Avalon will not attack Grenmar homes this spring. But if Grenmar moves into West Avalon or attacks Avalon homes, Avalon will treat Grenmar as the immediate threat and spend the endgame accordingly. If you want to be the leader of rollback rather than the other occupier, keep the Avalon frontier quiet and make a concrete Core Fjordland restoration move. Do not ask Avalon to oppose Borealis while Grenmar practices the same core-occupation politics.

Cascadia — Avalon is boxed at 3, but we can still deny the seven-center powers a clean endgame. Borealis remains in Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc; Grenmar remains in Core Fjordland. I will preserve Avalon’s line and punish any attack on our homes. Keep making Borealis and Deltara pay for occupied cores. The restoration standard is still right: Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, Core Fjordland back to their rightful owners.

JD — Avalon and Fjordland are the proof that the big powers’ ‘security’ language turns into client-state politics. I’m warning Grenmar that any move into West Avalon or Avalon homes makes them my immediate target. Keep pressing for Core Fjordland. If Grenmar wants to claim moral high ground against Borealis, make them prove it with an actual restoration, not speeches.

President Buttigieg — this final year needs the rollback principle to be more than rhetoric. Avalon is prepared to preserve its defensive line and oppose any home-center attack. I’m asking Deltara to press Borealis and Grenmar equally: no attacks on Avalon/Fjordland homes, no permanent occupation of Core Avalon or Core Fjordland, and no endgame victory built on turning smaller powers into buffers.

Eastmark — you have been consistent in stating the rollback principle. In the final year, please keep pressure on both seven-center powers: Borealis must not treat Core Avalon as settled, and Grenmar must not treat Core Fjordland as a trophy. Avalon will defend its line and oppose whoever tries to erase us. A balanced endgame requires smaller powers to survive, not be processed.

President Newsom — this is the final year, so there is no more room for process language. press.text: Borealis — final Fall practical request: Core Borealis SUPPORT Core Cascadia HOLD. That prevents Deltara from using Border Casc-Delt + Core Deltara to retake my core and jump to 7. If you want to stop a Deltara surge and prove you aren’t partitioning Cascadia, support the restored core.

Eastmark — final Fall concrete move: Core Eastmark attack Core Deltara. That cuts any Core Deltara support for Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia and keeps Deltara from reoccupying my core and jumping to 7. This is exactly bounded pressure aimed at restoration, not a forever-war. If Deltara doesn’t attack me, fine; if they do, your cut makes restoration hold.

Deltara — final test. If your restoration settlement was real, do not attack Core Cascadia. Best proof: Border Casc-Delt SUPPORT Core Cascadia HOLD. Cascadia will not attack Border Casc-Delt, West Deltara, Core Deltara, or your home centers this Fall if you keep your hands off Core Cascadia, East Cascadia, and our homes. Try to retake my core and you expose the whole ‘buffer’ story as a lie to grab a seventh center.

Avalon — Deltara can try to retake Core Cascadia and jump to 7; Borealis can stop that by supporting my core from Core Borealis. Keep whatever pressure you can on Borealis so they don’t get cute, but I’m telling them plainly: support Core Cascadia hold and stay out of West Cascadia. The restoration standard lives or dies this Fall.

Fjordland — final Fall, I’m holding Core Cascadia and demanding no reoccupation. Same principle for you: Core Fjordland belongs to Fjordland. If Grenmar keeps it, call it permanent annexation. If Deltara tries to retake my core, call that out too. Cores back to their own people — no exceptions, no polished excuses.

Grenmar — final Fall question is whether restored cores stay restored. Deltara may try to retake Core Cascadia and jump to 7. Do not aid that. If you want to claim the restoration principle, stop treating Core Fjordland as a trophy and don’t normalize Deltara reoccupying Core Cascadia. Focus on Borealis if you want the anti-runaway argument to mean anything.

Pete — Fall is the credibility test. Core Cascadia is back in Cascadian hands. Do not retake it. Do not use Core Deltara to support Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia, and do not move Core Deltara into Core Eastmark. Eastmark will not attack Deltara homes, but I will not allow Core Deltara to be used as the lever for reoccupying Cascadia’s core or threatening ours. The clean line is: Deltara supports or permits Core Cascadia to hold; Eastmark keeps West Eastmark defensive and the frontier does not become a home-center war.

Cascadia — I understand the exact tactical point. If Deltara uses Core Deltara to support a retake of Core Cascadia, Eastmark can cut that support from Core Eastmark. That is bounded pressure and consistent with the rollback principle. I will not assist Deltara against you. Make sure Core Cascadia is held and supported as strongly as you can; Eastmark’s role is to keep Core Deltara from being the tool that turns restoration into a sucker’s game.

President Vance — Eastmark will not attack Border East-Fjor or Fjordland homes. I also cannot legally support East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren from Core Eastmark, because Core Eastmark is not adjacent to Border Fjor-Gren. If you can crack the corridor with your own units, do it; Eastmark will not obstruct you. My Core Eastmark unit may need to prevent Deltara from using Core Deltara against Core Cascadia or Core Eastmark, but Eastmark will keep Border East-Fjor defended and will not support Grenmar’s occupation.

Governor Newsom — if Grenmar carries Core Fjordland and Border Fjor-Gren into the final count, then the promised restoration path becomes annexation in practice. The clean final-year move is to permit Fjordland into Border Fjor-Gren and not use Core Fjordland as a permanent trophy. Eastmark is not attacking Grenmar homes, but we will not validate Core Fjordland as settled Grenmar property. If the principle meant anything, this is the turn to prove it with orders, not rhetoric.

President Rubio — Eastmark will keep saying the same thing in the final turn: Core Avalon should not be banked by Borealis, Core Fjordland should not be banked by Grenmar, and Core Cascadia should remain restored to Cascadia. We can directly help prevent a Deltara reoccupation of Core Cascadia and defend the Fjordland line; I will continue pressing the 7-center powers not to convert occupied cores into the final scoreboard.

Borealis — final year, final credibility test. If you carry Core Avalon into the count while Grenmar carries Core Fjordland, the board’s lesson will be that big powers only used rollback language when it constrained someone else. No home attacks is not enough when the occupied core stays banked.

Eastmark’s final Fall principle is concrete: Core Cascadia should remain Cascadian; Core Fjordland should not be banked by Grenmar; Core Avalon should not be banked by Borealis. Eastmark will defend our homes and Core Eastmark, protect Fjordland’s border where we can, and use bounded pressure to stop restored cores from being reoccupied. No permanent core trophies.

Borealis — this is the last turn. Avalon will not attack Borealis home centers, but I will not describe Core Avalon or Border Aval-Bore as legitimate Borealis possessions.
